_about: Open Mind paper library. One record per paper or dataset. read_depth says whether the full text or only the abstract was read. verified=true means the DOI was opened and its title and authors matched (Crossref or DataCite, 2026-11-19); numbers come from the text that was read. Generated LIBRARY.md and site/library.html read this file.

papers.title: Alpha coherence is a network signature of cognitive recovery from disorders of consciousness
papers.authors: Zhou DW, Conte MM, Curley WH, Spencer-Salmon CA, Chatelle C, Rosenthal ES, Bodien YG, Victor JD, Schiff ND, Brown EN, Edlow BL
papers.question: Does the network organisation of posterior alpha coherence in clinical EEG track recovery of higher cognition after severe brain injury better than standard connectivity measures?
papers.tried: Alpha that stays in step across posterior cortex, summarised as a network, indexes the thalamocortical integrity needed for higher cognition.
papers.method_data: 95 clinical EEG recordings from two centres: 28 healthy controls and 33 patients with acute or chronic disorders of consciousness, 25 with follow-up. Global coherence analysis; network organisation from the principal eigenvector of the 8-12 Hz cross-spectral matrix. Recovery = CRS-R total 22 or above.
papers.key_results: Classifying recovery: AUC .78 for the alpha network measure against .45-.53 for weighted phase lag index connectivity (abstract only).
papers.limits: Small sample pooled from two studies; behavioural threshold outcome; published text closed, abstract only; an earlier medRxiv version gives slightly different comparison AUCs.
papers.ideas_for_us: Coherence comes from the cross-spectrum, which our multichannel phase-randomised surrogates keep, so it counts as spectral in the surrogate gate (#8). Test whether alpha network shape adds anything over alpha power on the Chennu propofol EEG (#21) under a sealed prereg.

papers.title: Neural signatures of conscious experience during sleep: a serial awakening study using high-density EEG
papers.authors: Selte A, Haworth SE, Vanasse TJ, Alauddin T, Gjini K, Philibert-Rosas S, Brace C, Sevak B, Riedner B, Kalkach-Aparicio M, Tononi G, Boly M, Struck AF
papers.question: Can EEG from the minute before an NREM awakening tell whether the sleeper will report a dream?
papers.tried: Dreaming should show as a posterior shift in spectral balance and in network organisation, as the posterior hot-zone account predicts.
papers.method_data: Overnight 256-electrode EEG in 140 participants, serial awakenings; 699 N2 and N3 awakenings (351 experience, 348 no experience). Features from the 60 s before waking: regional spectral power, lagged coherence, graph metrics, gamma-to-alpha ratios. Participant-level cross-validated classifiers.
papers.key_results: Dreaming went with lower posterior alpha and delta power and higher gamma-related measures. All classifiers beat chance; the best ensemble reached ROC-AUC 0.80 and average precision 0.80. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Abstract only: the bioRxiv full text was not reachable without getting around a bot block. N2 and N3 are pooled, so sleep depth can carry part of the signal: in another serial-awakening cohort no-experience reports were 50% of N3 but 21.9% of N2 awakenings (Bertoni 2026). One lab, no cross-lab test, no spectral-baseline nesting, no surrogate gate. Licence is no-reuse; data availability not stated in the abstract.
papers.ideas_for_us: This is the strongest claim yet against our 'markers fail on experience' outcome. Our #42 design holds stage fixed (N2), holds labs out and nests every marker in the frozen spectral baseline, so it answers the question this paper leaves open: does the 0.80 survive stage control and a new lab? Report the spectral baseline's own experience AUC as a headline number, because if it is near 0.80 the 'bounded below 0.60' negative applies only to non-spectral markers. Check whether this cohort contains the 39 Wisconsin subjects of the DREAM Tononi set (same lab); that set is already in our exposed tier.

papers.title: Neural correlates of dreaming during N2 sleep: spatial and phenomenological characteristics
papers.authors: Rochas V, Mammeri K, Bayer L, Tononi G, Perogamvros L
papers.question: Where and when does N2 EEG differ between awakenings with and without a dream, and does it track the kind of experience?
papers.tried: Extend the posterior hot-zone finding to a larger N2 sample with source localisation, and split experience into perceptual and thought-like dimensions.
papers.method_data: 256-electrode EEG with source localisation, serial awakenings in N2, 39 participants; several pre-awakening windows; continuous ratings of perceptual and thought-related experience.
papers.key_results: Experience with recall vs no experience went with higher beta/gamma over a wide cortical area, peaking in posterior occipito-temporal cortex for the 30 s window and in parietal cortex for the 20 s window. Thought-related ratings, not perceptual ones, were associated with EEG activity. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Abstract only. One lab, 39 people, no held-out test. The preprint's title and framing changed across versions (v1 'The neural generators of perceptual experiences during sleep', v2 'Content-specific and temporally evolving neural correlates'), so the analysis path may have moved.
papers.ideas_for_us: Our #42 window is the last 20 s, which is where they place the effect over parietal cortex; their high-frequency effect is exactly what our frozen spectral baseline (with 20-50 Hz power) should absorb. If DREAM packages carry content ratings, 'thought vs perception' could become a sealed secondary label in a later study, not this one.

papers.title: Immersive NREM2 dreaming preserves subjective sleep depth against declining sleep pressure
papers.authors: Michalak A, Marzoli D, Pietrogiacomi F, Bergamo D, Elce V, Pedreschi B, Mosca G, Navari A, et al.
papers.question: How do cortical activation and the kind of dream relate to how deeply people feel they slept?
papers.tried: Feeling of deep sleep is usually read as unconsciousness; immersive dreaming might instead keep sleep feeling deep.
papers.method_data: Two N2 serial-awakening experiments at IMT Lucca, four nights each, high-density EEG; 1,024 N2 awakenings with reports, sleep-depth and sleepiness ratings. Five report classes (experience with recall, rich and simple experience without recall, experience of sleep, unconsciousness). Channel-wise delta and gamma power and their ratio.
papers.key_results: Deeper perceived sleep went with lower high-to-low frequency power ratio, and this link weakened when a dream was present. The immersive quality of the experience was tied to perceived depth whether or not content was recalled. Data and code are open: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.15372992 (CC BY 4.0) holds a per-awakening table of channel-wise delta and gamma power plus the cluster statistics (derivatives 180 MB), not raw EEG.
papers.limits: Derived spectral features only, so complexity or connectivity markers cannot be computed. One lab. Report categories differ from DREAM's three-way coding.
papers.ideas_for_us: New open data for #42: an eighth, never-touched lab with 1,024 N2 awakenings. It can test the spectral side only (does posterior gamma/delta separate experience from unconsciousness at N2 in a new lab?). That is a direct out-of-lab check on the spectral baseline that Selte 2026 implies may already be strong. Needs a sealed amendment before anyone opens the labels.

papers.title: From high- to low-density EEG for automatic classification of dream experiences during stage 2 of NREM
papers.authors: Moctezuma LA, Molinas M, Abe T
papers.question: Can machine learning classify N2 dream vs no-dream awakenings from EEG, and with how few channels?
papers.tried: Train classifiers on 256-channel EEG and prune channels.
papers.method_data: DREAM Tononi serial-awakening set (doi 10.26180/23306054.v2): 261 N2 reports (110 experience, 101 no experience, 50 experience without recall), 2 min before waking. 70/30 split and 10-fold cross-validation over awakenings; KNN.
papers.key_results: Accuracy up to 0.94 and ROC-AUC 0.97; performance held with 30-40 channels. Experience-without-recall awakenings were classed as experience 0.698 of the time.
papers.limits: Splits are over awakenings, not subjects, so a person's EEG signature can sit in both train and test. The near-perfect AUC is very likely inflated by subject leakage; compare Wong 2025 (AUC 0.59 in NREM, held out) and the authors' own leave-one-subject-out failure in Moctezuma 2025 (BMRI).
papers.ideas_for_us: A ready red-team example for #42: rerun this pipeline subject-held-out on the Tononi set (exposed tier) to show how much of 0.97 is leakage. It also supports our rule that no awakening-level split is ever reported.

papers.title: Unlocking dreams and dreamless sleep: machine learning classification with optimal EEG channels
papers.authors: Moctezuma LA, Molinas M, Abe T
papers.question: Can EEG classify dream vs dreamless awakenings, and which channels matter?
papers.tried: Common spatial patterns and wavelet features with KNN, then channel selection.
papers.method_data: DREAM Zhang & Wamsley set: 58 channels, 28 subjects, REM and NREM awakenings.
papers.key_results: Accuracies above 0.85 with pooled data; 8-10 channels looked sufficient. When one subject at a time was held out, the models failed to generalise to unseen subjects.
papers.limits: The headline accuracy is not subject-held-out; the held-out result, which is the one that matters, is weak.
papers.ideas_for_us: Independent evidence, on one of our exposed-tier labs, that dream decoding collapses under subject hold-out. Cite it next to Wong 2025 when stating priors for #42.

papers.title: The neural basis of consciousness during evening naps measured by MEG: a registered report
papers.authors: Hemmi C, Leung A, Windt J, Motomura Y, et al.
papers.question: Do the posterior low- and high-frequency correlates of dreaming from a landmark EEG study generalise to MEG during evening naps?
papers.tried: A registered report: hypotheses about frontal and posterior low- and high-frequency power fixed before an independent team analyses the data.
papers.method_data: MEG with targeted serial awakenings during naps; Stage 1 (protocol) accepted with pilot data from two participants.
papers.key_results: In one pilot participant the low-frequency hypotheses held and the high-frequency ones did not; the other gave insufficient evidence. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Stage 2 results not out yet. Naps, not full nights.
papers.ideas_for_us: A pre-registered, independent replication of the same posterior signature our #42 spectral controls include. When Stage 2 appears, compare its effect sizes with ours.

papers.title: Multisensory integration in peripersonal space indexes consciousness states in sleep and disorders of consciousness
papers.authors: Bertoni T, Ricci G, Jöhr J, Donno B, Cataldi J, et al.
papers.question: Does an EEG index of peripersonal-space processing track consciousness across wake, dreaming, dreamless sleep and brain injury?
papers.tried: A minimal-self (body-space) index should be present whenever experience is, regardless of behaviour.
papers.method_data: 256-channel EEG during an audiotactile near/far paradigm in wake and overnight with about 9 serial awakenings a night; then 72 DoC patients at the bedside.
papers.key_results: A centro-parietal high-beta (20-30 Hz) index separated near from far stimuli in wake and in dreaming, not dreamless sleep. Experience reports rose from N3 (32.1%) to N2 (56.2%) to REM (87.9%); no-experience fell from N3 (50%) to N2 (21.9%) to REM (0%). In 72 patients, CRS-R plus the index predicted outcome with accuracy 0.85 (CRS-R alone 0.82).
papers.limits: Stimulus-evoked, so not usable on spontaneous DREAM recordings. EEG data cannot be deposited. The stage-by-report table shows how strongly stage and report co-vary.
papers.ideas_for_us: Its stage-by-report numbers are the cleanest argument for holding stage fixed in #42 (and the reason Selte 2026's pooled N2+N3 AUC may be inflated). A stimulus-based experience marker is out of scope for our spontaneous-EEG benchmark.

papers.title: Dreaming during anaesthesia: a scoping review
papers.authors: Sikka P, Hu S, Heifets BD
papers.question: How often do people dream under anaesthesia, and what predicts it?
papers.tried: Pool a century of studies on anaesthesia dreaming.
papers.method_data: Scoping review of 157 studies (1921-2024), 87,866 participants.
papers.key_results: Recall was 40-80% in experimental settings and 3-8% in large clinical trials. Ketamine and propofol were most consistently associated with recall. Recall was not associated with intraoperative awareness. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Heterogeneous methods; recall depends heavily on when and how people are asked.
papers.ideas_for_us: Propofol dreaming is common enough that 'unresponsive' does not mean 'no experience', which is why our state benchmark (Study 2) only claims arousal, not experience, for propofol contrasts.

papers.title: Feasibility of a multicomponent protocol to promote dreaming during surgical anesthesia
papers.authors: Sikka P, Ngo MC, Hu S, Wilkerson TB, Shull M, Imbordino K, Ishii T, Kawai M, Deverett B, Chow HS, Heifets BD
papers.question: Can routine anaesthesia be steered towards dreaming at emergence?
papers.tried: Priming, propofol emergence, EEG-guided quiet emergence and immediate interviews should raise dream recall.
papers.method_data: Prospective quality-improvement study, 474 surgical patients, SedLine EEG monitoring.
papers.key_results: 69% of 452 interviewed patients reported dreaming; 93% of 57 with full protocol adherence. Dreamers rated sleep quality higher (9.16 vs 7.65). No intraoperative awareness. (abstract only)
papers.limits: No dream/no-dream EEG analysis reported in the abstract; EEG is a 4-channel clinical monitor.
papers.ideas_for_us: If emergence EEG with dream reports is ever shared, it would give a propofol 'experience at fixed state' contrast, a third arm beside NREM and REM for #42-style tests.

papers.title: Using real-time reporting to investigate visual experiences in dreams
papers.authors: Konkoly KR, Al-Youssef S, Mazurek CY, Mallett R, Morris DJ, Gales A, Arnulf I, Oudiette D, Paller KA
papers.question: Do lucid dreamers' signalled visual experiences line up with alpha power as in waking?
papers.tried: Real-time sniff signals during REM avoid the distortion of reports given after waking.
papers.method_data: 13 lucid dreamers (4 with narcolepsy); 150 signals over 19 sessions from 11 people.
papers.key_results: No robust alpha increase after signalled dream eye closure; dream eye closure faded visual content only about half the time. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Very small n; lucid REM only.
papers.ideas_for_us: A reminder for #42's stated limit (report is not experience): post-waking reports are coarse. Not usable data for us.

papers.title: Thalamic contributions to predictive coding and disconnected consciousness in human volunteers
papers.authors: Wehrman JJ, Casey C, Redinbaugh MJ, Muller E, Munn B, et al.
papers.question: Does the cortex stop synchronising to surprising sounds when consciousness is disconnected from the world?
papers.tried: Disconnected consciousness (dreaming-like) should reduce surprise-driven cortical synchrony.
papers.method_data: 18 volunteers, auditory oddball, EEG, awake vs dexmedetomidine sedation with disconnection confirmed by serial awakening.
papers.key_results: Surprise was more strongly expressed in awake EEG, with frontal negative (33-356 ms) and posterior positive (37-400 ms) effects that diminished in disconnection; voxel coactivation also dropped (P<0.001). (abstract only)
papers.limits: Evoked paradigm; small n; data availability not stated in the abstract.
papers.ideas_for_us: Shows serial awakenings can confirm 'disconnected but experiencing' under sedation; a model for a future sedation arm of the experience benchmark.

papers.title: Increased intra-thalamic and thalamo-cortical functional connections during human REM sleep: a two-night EEG-fMRI study
papers.authors: Yang FN, Picchioni D, de Zwart JA, van Gelderen P, Duyn JH
papers.question: How does the thalamus connect to sensory networks during REM, when vivid dreams occur?
papers.tried: Phasic REM, linked to vivid dreaming, should show more thalamic broadcasting than tonic REM.
papers.method_data: Whole-night EEG-fMRI in 12 participants; HMM split of phasic and tonic REM.
papers.key_results: Intra-thalamic connectivity was higher in REM than wake in all 11 participants with good REM fMRI, and higher than NREM in 9 of 11; phasic REM exceeded tonic REM. (abstract only)
papers.limits: No dream reports; phasic REM is a proxy for vividness.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context for REM in #42; a phasic/tonic split is a possible covariate if REM awakenings are analysed.

papers.title: EEG microstates reveal distinct network dynamics in lucid and non-lucid REM sleep
papers.authors: Wang X, Peters E, Strelen J, Lockhart N, Franklin M, LaBerge S, Koenig T, Dresler M, Erlacher D
papers.question: Do EEG microstates differ between lucid and non-lucid REM?
papers.tried: Lucidity should shift large-scale network states towards metacognitive ones.
papers.method_data: EEG microstate analysis of lucid vs non-lucid REM.
papers.key_results: Microstates A and G dominated lucid REM; B, C and D were reduced. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Sample size not in the abstract; lucidity is a content change, not presence vs absence of experience.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context only.

papers.title: Intra-thalamic coordination maintains arousability in slow-wave sleep
papers.authors: Han J, Xie Q, Huang Y, Li M, Hu X, Northoff G, Li Y, Zhang J, Qin P
papers.question: How do thalamic nuclei keep a sleeper wakeable during slow-wave sleep?
papers.tried: A centromedian-VPL-pulvinar loop preserves arousability, unlike anaesthesia or UWS.
papers.method_data: Six fMRI and EEG datasets spanning sleep, propofol and unresponsive wakefulness.
papers.key_results: In N2/N3, CM and VPL showed convergent edge communities and more closed-loop intra-thalamic motifs, not seen under anaesthesia or UWS. CM->VPL->pulvinar connectivity rose in N3 and covaried with N3 delta power, which was higher before awakenings than before transitions to N2 and went with 3-month improvement in UWS. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Abstract only; preprint; fMRI-heavy.
papers.ideas_for_us: Arousability is a separate axis from experience. In #42, delta before waking is in the baseline; this paper suggests delta may index how close the sleeper is to waking, a covariate worth reporting.

papers.title: Spontaneous slow waves index multiple dimensions of recovery in disorders of consciousness
papers.authors: Ruyant Belabbas A, Boullet A, Manasova D, Le Coz A, Valente M, Lejeune F, Sitt JD, Naccache L, Rohaut B, Andrillon T
papers.question: Do local slow waves in DoC patients index damage, residual awareness, or recovery potential?
papers.tried: Sleep-like slow waves in awake patients may carry information about cortical state beyond EEG slowing.
papers.method_data: 256-channel EEG during the Local-Global paradigm in 236 DoC patients (123 UWS, 62 MCS-, 29 MCS+); slow-wave density, amplitude and slopes, related to CRS-R, Local-Global responses, one-year GOS-E and MRI.
papers.key_results: Associations with concurrent and follow-up measures are reported; the abstract text available to us was cut before the numerical results. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Abstract only; data availability unknown; no open DoC EEG.
papers.ideas_for_us: Slow-wave density and slope belong on our arousal axis. If the Paris DoC EEG ever opens, Study 2's DoC arm could test whether complexity markers add anything over slow-wave features.

papers.title: Individualised electrophysiological neural field models for the assessment of thalamocortical function in disorders of consciousness: a multicentre study
papers.authors: Cóngyǔ L, Tewarie PKB, Alnagger NLN, Mindlin I, Van der Lande GJM, Belloli L, Laureys S, Naccache L, Rohaut B, Thibaut A, Annen J, Gosseries O, Núñez P, Sitt JD
papers.question: Can a fitted corticothalamic model explain EEG differences between MCS and UWS?
papers.tried: Per-patient corticothalamic neural field fits should reveal reduced thalamocortical integrity (mesocircuit hypothesis).
papers.method_data: High-density EEG from two independent datasets: 203 UWS, 270 MCS, 74 controls; Robinson model fitted to spectra; simulated EEG compared on complexity metrics.
papers.key_results: The model captured spectral features across states and showed reduced corticothalamic integrity, worse in UWS than MCS. Simulated EEG reproduced empirical complexity; permutation entropy distinguished MCS from UWS in real and simulated data. Code and replication data on GitHub (braintrak, nftsim, predictivecat/DoC_tcmodel).
papers.limits: A model fitted to the spectrum reproduces complexity, which means complexity here is largely spectral.
papers.ideas_for_us: Strong support for our spectral-confound line: if a spectrum-fitted model reproduces permutation entropy, PE carries little beyond the spectrum. Check whether the DoC_tcmodel repository holds per-patient fitted parameters or spectra; if so, it is the first open DoC-derived data for Study 2.

papers.title: Thermodynamics of consciousness: non-equilibrium brain dynamics track conscious states
papers.authors: Berjaga-Buisan T, Monti JM, Cortada M, Colombo MA, Geli SM, Gaglioti G, Sarasso S, Kringelbach ML, Corbetta M, Sanchez-Vives MV, Massimini M, Perl YS, Deco G
papers.question: Does non-equilibrium in spontaneous brain activity track consciousness the way PCI does?
papers.tried: Violations of the fluctuation-dissipation theorem (FDT), estimated from whole-brain models fitted to spontaneous signals, should fall with loss of consciousness.
papers.method_data: Generative whole-brain models in humans (wake, anaesthesia, DoC) and mice (graded anaesthesia, LFP).
papers.key_results: In mice PCI tracked anaesthesia depth (Spearman 0.71), FDT violations tracked it more tightly (0.885), and FDT correlated with PCI (0.68). FDT violations fell in unresponsive DoC and anaesthesia. Mouse LFP data are open on EBRAINS (10.25493/WKA8-Q4T).
papers.limits: Model-based, not compared against a spectral baseline. Anaesthesia and DoC confound arousal with consciousness.
papers.ideas_for_us: We already tested its scalp second-order irreversibility form (ne2) and it did not replicate (AUC 0.43-0.56); our higher-order variant tracked arousal only. The model-based FDT estimator is still untested by us and would need the spectral baseline and an arousal-free contrast such as #42's.

papers.title: Inferring brain structural complexity from dynamical measures
papers.authors: Gaglioti G, Cattani A, Nieus T, Momi D, Comolatti R, Dalla Porta L, Sarasso S, Massimini M
papers.question: Which complexity measures actually reflect the integration-differentiation balance of the underlying network?
papers.tried: Simulate networks with known structure and see which observational and perturbational measures follow it.
papers.method_data: Wilson-Cowan mean-field simulations over systematically rewired networks; observational (spontaneous) and perturbational metrics.
papers.key_results: Observational measures behaved heterogeneously: some tracked integration, some differentiation, some barely moved. Perturbational measures peaked at intermediate rewiring, scaled with small-worldness, resisted common-driver confounds and were highest near a wake-like regime. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Simulation only; abstract only.
papers.ideas_for_us: A model-based reason why the spontaneous-EEG markers in #42 may fail: they do not track structure reliably. Use it to frame a negative #42 result, and as a design idea: plant structure in simulation as a positive control for each marker.

papers.title: Waveform morphology links local circuit kinetics to cortical interactions
papers.authors: Núñez P, Kumar G, Gotti C, Wang P, Martineau L, Bonaventure PL, Hoyer R, Mišić B, Albouy P, Laureys S, Tewarie PKB
papers.question: How does local synaptic kinetics shape waveform shape and measures of inter-areal interaction?
papers.tried: Synaptic rise and decay times set waveform asymmetry, which then biases irreversibility and coherence measures.
papers.method_data: Modified Wilson-Cowan model; stereo-EEG from 23 patients; macaque ECoG.
papers.key_results: Waveform asymmetry was most strongly associated with local irreversibility in sEEG; alpha frequency related more to inter-regional measures. Phase-locked perturbations changed imaginary coherency and irreversibility with coupling fixed. Macaque ECoG reproduced the frequency links but not the waveform link. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Abstract only; preprint.
papers.ideas_for_us: A mechanism for our own result: our waveform-asymmetry marker tra_x separated wake from N3 but not REM from N3. If asymmetry indexes local kinetics, it should track arousal-linked synaptic changes, not experience. Cite it in the nonequilibrium write-up.

papers.title: Pharmacological evidence for propagation dynamics of TMS-evoked potentials in the human brain
papers.authors: Bai Z, Belardinelli P, Gordon PC, Ziemann U
papers.question: Which GABA-A drugs change early (feedforward) vs late (recurrent) TMS-evoked propagation, and PCI?
papers.tried: Early beta-band coupling changes should drive later recurrent spread and PCI.
papers.method_data: Placebo-controlled crossover TMS-EEG with zolpidem, alprazolam and diazepam, plus active vs sham TMS.
papers.key_results: Alprazolam lowered early beta-band coupling and, in the late stage, current density, scattering and PCI-lz; zolpidem raised early current density but left coupling and PCI-lz unchanged; diazepam replicated alprazolam. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Healthy awake volunteers; sedation, not loss of consciousness.
papers.ideas_for_us: PCI-lz moves with some GABA-A drugs and not others at similar sedation, a reminder that PCI tracks circuit pharmacology as well as consciousness. Relevant to how we grade PCI-based constraints in the ledger.

papers.title: Assessing consciousness by near-nerve electrostimulation in intensive rehabilitation
papers.authors: Liuzzi P, Ballanti S, Mannini A, Hakiki B, Burali R, Toci T, Carrozza MC, Oddo CM, Grippo A
papers.question: Does near-nerve median stimulation give a better EEG marker of consciousness in prolonged DoC than surface stimulation?
papers.tried: Selective sensory activation without motor recruitment should give cleaner evoked complexity.
papers.method_data: 19 prolonged DoC patients, high-density EEG, evoked potentials, field power and perturbational complexity.
papers.key_results: A combined index classified chronic unresponsive patients with leave-one-subject-out accuracy 94.7% (95% CI 77.9-99.4%), sensitivity 100%, specificity 90.9%; surface stimulation gave 63.2%. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Single-centre pilot of 19; internal cross-validation only, as the authors say.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context. Small-n perfect-looking classifiers are exactly what our held-out rules guard against.

papers.title: Altered temporal dynamics of resting-state EEG microstates as a neural signature of impaired consciousness: a high-density EEG analysis in chronic disorders of consciousness
papers.authors: Dong X, Wang D, Hou J, Wang P, Jian X, Feng T
papers.question: Can EEG microstates separate UWS from MCS?
papers.tried: Microstate D coverage should fall with frontoparietal decoupling.
papers.method_data: High-density resting EEG in 20 UWS, 22 MCS and 20 controls; control-derived templates; leave-one-subject-out logistic regression.
papers.key_results: Class D coverage fell from controls to MCS to UWS. (abstract only; the abstract's statistics were truncated)
papers.limits: Small; single site.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context.

papers.title: The diagnostic and prognostic value of auditory statistical learning ability in patients with disorders of consciousness
papers.authors: Yu M, Xiao X, Ding J, Zhao M, Cruz S, Hu N, Zhang M, Laureys S, Di H, Chen Y
papers.question: Is neural tracking of statistical regularities preserved in DoC and does it predict outcome?
papers.tried: Frequency-tagged entrainment to trisyllabic pseudowords indexes residual cognition.
papers.method_data: EEG in 46 patients and 25 controls.
papers.key_results: Controls and MCS showed the learning effect, UWS did not; the effect predicted behavioural scores in MCS and 6-month outcome in traumatic patients. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Small; task-based.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context.

papers.title: Decoding sequence auditory expectations for clinical diagnostic and prognostic assessment of prolonged disorders of consciousness
papers.authors: Luo R, Huang Y, Xue C, Yu QY, Hu N, Wei Y, Liu H, Laureys SD, Di H, Meng J
papers.question: Can single-trial decoding of global auditory regularities assess prolonged DoC?
papers.tried: A lower-demand Local-Global variant and single-trial classifiers.
papers.method_data: Modified Local-Global paradigm; CCA, PCA and xDAWN feature pipelines; healthy and DoC participants.
papers.key_results: Single-trial classification of global effects improved by up to 15% over the original paradigm in healthy participants. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Abstract does not give patient numbers.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context.

papers.title: Covert consciousness in behavioral coma
papers.authors: Edlow BL, Fecchio M, Freeman HJ, Rapalino O, Cash SS, Young MJ
papers.question: Can a patient who looks comatose (eyes closed) show task-based covert consciousness?
papers.tried: Awareness may dissociate from wakefulness.
papers.method_data: Single case, acute severe TBI, task-based fMRI and EEG.
papers.key_results: An 80-year-old woman in behavioural coma on every exam showed covert consciousness on both task fMRI and task EEG. The authors cite about 25% covert consciousness among unresponsive patients. (abstract only)
papers.limits: One case.
papers.ideas_for_us: Adds to ledger constraint on covert consciousness: wakefulness is not a precondition, which weakens arousal-as-proxy logic in clinical claims.

papers.title: Covert consciousness is not cognitive motor dissociation and the vegetative state is not a state of mind
papers.authors: Monti M, Schnakers C, Schiff N, Bodien Y
papers.question: Is DoC nosology coherent once covert consciousness is known?
papers.tried: Diagnostic categories mix inferred experience with observed behaviour; CC and CMD identify different patients.
papers.method_data: Conceptual analysis.
papers.key_results: Argues that equating unresponsiveness with unconsciousness is a category error that blocks clinical use of imaging and EEG findings. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Opinion.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context for how we label DoC ground truth in any Study 2 DoC arm.

papers.title: Intravenous methylphenidate for acute traumatic disorders of consciousness: a phase 1 dose-finding and target engagement study
papers.authors: Edlow BL, Barra ME, Schreier DR, Fecchio M, et al.
papers.question: Is IV methylphenidate safe in acute traumatic DoC, and does it engage brain networks?
papers.tried: Dopaminergic stimulation may reactivate subcortical arousal networks.
papers.method_data: Open-label phase 1, 9 male ICU patients (3 coma, 3 VS/UWS, 3 MCS), 0.5-2.0 mg/kg; EEG and rs-fMRI change-point analysis.
papers.key_results: No serious adverse events at any dose; mild-moderate events at higher doses. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Tiny, open-label.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context.

papers.title: Functional fractionation of large-scale brain networks in the human subcortex
papers.authors: Li J, Atalay AS, Olchanyi MD, Cambareri MK, Ghosh SS, Horn A, Lewis LD, Brown EN, Fischl B, Kinney HC, Edlow BL
papers.question: Can subcortical network components be separated in resting fMRI?
papers.tried: A tensor decomposition (NASCAR) to split overlapping networks.
papers.method_data: Resting fMRI from 1,000 HCP participants; proof of principle in severe TBI.
papers.key_results: Four large networks split into 15 reproducible subnetworks; individual subnetwork patterns predicted level of consciousness in severe TBI. (abstract only)
papers.limits: fMRI.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context.

papers.title: Resting-state functional MRI and clinical outcomes after acute disorders of consciousness: a systematic review
papers.authors: Kazazian K, Czink D, Iansavitchene A, Owen AM, Norton L
papers.question: Does resting fMRI in the acute phase predict outcome after severe brain injury?
papers.tried: Systematic review.
papers.method_data: 30 of 396 screened studies; 800 patients.
papers.key_results: Default mode (20 studies) and executive control networks (11) were most assessed. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Abstract truncated before conclusions.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context.

papers.title: Pharmacological treatments in disorders of consciousness
papers.authors: Saleh C, Seyfzadeh F, Szymkowicz E, Alnagger N, Ilia TS, Oancea AA, Gosseries O
papers.question: What drugs help recovery of consciousness in DoC?
papers.tried: Narrative review.
papers.method_data: Dopaminergic, GABAergic and other agents; RCTs and lower-class evidence.
papers.key_results: Improvements are inconsistent; 12 of 22 RCTs (about 55%) had some concerns or high risk of bias. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Narrative.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context.

papers.title: Mapping basal ganglia circuitry in altered states of consciousness: from pathology to pharmacology
papers.authors: Szocs D, Luppi AI, Coppola P, Adapa R, Williams GB, Allanson J, Pickard JD, Owen AM, Naci L, Menon DK, Stamatakis EA
papers.question: How do basal ganglia nuclei and neurotransmitter systems change in propofol and DoC loss of responsiveness?
papers.tried: Map 9 nuclei against 19 transmitter systems.
papers.method_data: fMRI, 16 volunteers under propofol, 22 DoC patients.
papers.key_results: Putamen changes correlated with the noradrenaline transporter and GPe with serotonin and acetylcholine transporters under propofol. (abstract only)
papers.limits: fMRI; small.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context.

papers.title: Opposite network patterns of integration-segregation in psychedelic and sedated states of consciousness
papers.authors: Dai R, Jang H, Hudetz AG, Huang Z, Mashour GA
papers.question: Do psychedelic and sedated states shift brain network integration and segregation in opposite directions?
papers.tried: A mirror-image hypothesis: psychedelics integrate, sleep and propofol segregate.
papers.method_data: fMRI across psychedelics, sleep and propofol; several connectivity, topology and complexity measures. Data: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.14029241, OpenNeuro ds003768 (sleep fMRI) and ds003059 (LSD).
papers.key_results: Psychedelics showed more integration and less segregation; sleep and propofol the opposite; the pattern held across spatial scales and data-driven classifiers.
papers.limits: fMRI only; arousal and drug effects are confounded with consciousness in every contrast.
papers.ideas_for_us: A clean prediction for Study 2's state axis on EEG: if integration measures (wSMI, total correlation) flip sign between psilocybin (ds006110) and propofol, they track something other than plain arousal.

papers.title: Psychedelics align brain activity with context
papers.authors: Stoliker D, Novelli L, Khajehnejad M, Biabani M, Greaves MD, et al.
papers.question: What brain organisation underlies the self- and boundary-dissolving experiences of psilocybin, and how does context shape it?
papers.tried: Low-dimensional trajectories, not time averages, should reveal structured, context-aligned dynamics.
papers.method_data: 62 adults, fMRI (about 80 min post-dose) and 64-channel EEG (about 150 min post-dose) during rest, meditation, music and movie, before and on the day of psilocybin. Open data: OpenNeuro ds006110 (v1.2.0).
papers.key_results: Psilocybin reorganised activity into structured, context-sensitive trajectories that co-varied with experience; networks that usually segregate internal and external processing integrated in people reporting 'embeddedness'. Half ranked the experience among the most meaningful of their lives.
papers.limits: Single site; EEG was recorded later than fMRI; no placebo session on the drug day as described in the abstract.
papers.ideas_for_us: New open data for Study 2: a psychedelic EEG set with rest and naturalistic tasks and experience ratings, on OpenNeuro. It is the 'expanded experience, no arousal loss' contrast our state benchmark lacks; markers that rise here and fall under propofol pass a test that wake vs N3 cannot set.

papers.title: Emergent multiscale organisation of neural dynamics fragments in anaesthesia
papers.authors: Milinkovic B, Seth AK, Barnett L, Carter O, Andrillon T
papers.question: How does emergent multiscale organisation change under propofol, xenon and ketamine?
papers.tried: Dynamical independence (DI) should separate drugs that abolish report from ketamine, which keeps dream-like experience.
papers.method_data: Source-reconstructed 61-channel EEG from the Milan cohort (Sarasso 2015): 14 adults, propofol 4, xenon 5, ketamine 5.
papers.key_results: Propofol and xenon showed more emergence but highly variable, fragmented macroscopic structure; ketamine showed less emergence with partial preservation of structure. The authors warn against equating emergence with level of consciousness.
papers.limits: n = 4-5 per drug, the same single cohort behind most ketamine claims. The paper calls the data open-access; our record has Zenodo 806176 as restricted (access requested 18 Nov 2026).
papers.ideas_for_us: Another measure that dissociates ketamine from propofol on the one Milan cohort; it does not change our ketamine gap. Worth asking whether DI survives the spectral baseline.

papers.title: Psilocybin-induced changes in electroencephalography link acute and long-term effects
papers.authors: Nikolič M, Froese T, Mediano PAM, Koudelka V, Horáček J, Tylš F, Páleníček T
papers.question: How do psilocybin's EEG effects unfold over 24 hours and do they predict lasting change?
papers.tried: Acute entropy rises track acute experience; sub-acute spectral shifts track long-term outcomes.
papers.method_data: Double-blind placebo-controlled crossover, N = 20, about 0.26 mg/kg, high-density resting EEG at baseline, 1, 3, 6 and 24 h, 28-day follow-up.
papers.key_results: Alpha/beta power fell and gamma-band signal diversity rose at 1-3 h; gamma diversity correlated with acute psychological effects (r = 0.71). At 24 h reduced delta/theta correlated with positive life changes at 4 weeks (r = -0.47 to -0.57). (abstract only)
papers.limits: Small; diversity not tested against a spectral baseline.
papers.ideas_for_us: A within-subject case where a complexity measure tracks experience intensity while arousal stays wake-like. If the data were open it would be a #42-style test; ask whether gamma diversity survives band-power nesting.

papers.title: The entropic brain today
papers.authors: Carhart-Harris RL
papers.question: How well has the entropic brain hypothesis held up?
papers.tried: Brain entropy scales with the 'size' of phenomenal consciousness, separately from arousal.
papers.method_data: Narrative review of evidence across psychedelics, meditation, REM, DoC, sleep, anaesthesia, ageing and disease.
papers.key_results: Claims convergent, correlative, predictive, discriminative and external validity, and that entropy changes selectively index the breadth of experience rather than arousal. LZ on EEG/MEG is named the go-to metric. The review itself says increased high-frequency activity is a major carrier of the entropic brain effect.
papers.limits: A proponent's review. It does not test entropy against a spectral baseline, although it concedes high-frequency power carries much of the effect; the discriminative-validity claim rests mainly on psychedelic fMRI contrasts.
papers.ideas_for_us: Our results speak to this directly: LZ adds nothing over the spectrum in sleep and fails the surrogate gate. #42 tests the 'not arousal' claim at fixed sleep stage. A sealed prediction from this review (entropy higher before experience awakenings, beyond spectrum) belongs in #42's measure list, which already includes LZ and entropy measures.

papers.title: State-dependent, frequency-specific modulation of electrocortical traveling waves by anesthesia
papers.authors: Li D, Hudetz AG
papers.question: How does anaesthesia change cortical travelling waves?
papers.tried: Travelling-wave structure should change with depth and with spontaneous state transitions.
papers.method_data: Hemispheric ECoG in rats at 6, 4, 2 and 0% desflurane.
papers.key_results: Delta-band waves became more frequent and stereotyped (more planar, fewer source/sink) at 4-6%; theta and gamma wave rates were largely unchanged; a paradoxical awake-like state in deep anaesthesia partly shifted towards wake patterns. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Rats; abstract only.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context.

papers.title: Thalamic modulation of cortical linearity across arousal states
papers.authors: Müller EJ, Munn BR, Baracchini G, Fulcher BD, et al.
papers.question: Does the thalamus regulate how linear or nonlinear cortical dynamics are?
papers.tried: A time-resolved linearity measure should fluctuate along a thalamic axis and fall with lost arousal.
papers.method_data: Human fMRI and electrophysiology, macaque recordings, pharmacological ablation of arousal and thalamic stimulation.
papers.key_results: Awake cortex showed irregular linearity fluctuations following a thalamic anatomical axis; they diminished when arousal was pharmacologically ablated and recovered with thalamic stimulation. (abstract only)
papers.limits: An arousal measure by construction.
papers.ideas_for_us: Linearity is another candidate for the arousal axis; it should be scored on Study 2, not claimed as an experience marker.

papers.title: Brain network dynamics in the wake-sleep transition reorganize according to task engagement
papers.authors: Kumar SS, Arzi A, Bareham CA, Gonzalez-Castillo J, Fernandez I, Tagliazucchi E, Mediano PAM, Bandettini PA, Bekinschtein TA
papers.question: How do falling alertness and task engagement interact in shared circuits?
papers.tried: Active engagement during drowsiness should recruit frontoparietal and sensory networks while thalamocortical sleep-onset changes continue.
papers.method_data: EEG-fMRI, people drifting between alert and drowsy states during active or passive auditory tasks.
papers.key_results: With falling alertness, passive listening raised parietal synchrony and thalamo-cortical synchrony; active engagement raised long-range frontoparietal synchrony and auditory-cortex coupling instead. (abstract only)
papers.limits: fMRI-heavy.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context for sleep-onset (N1) analyses; our #34 sleep-onset sign-flip theory could cite it.

papers.title: Abnormal local markers of sleep homeostasis in patients with focal epilepsy
papers.authors: Ciliento R, Sevak B, Papantonatos C, et al.
papers.question: Is sleep homeostasis altered in focal epilepsy?
papers.tried: Slow-wave activity and slope should decline less overnight in epilepsy.
papers.method_data: Overnight 256-electrode EEG in 39 patients and 48 matched controls.
papers.key_results: Patients had higher slow-wave activity and steeper slopes; their end-of-night values resembled controls' start-of-night values. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Clinical population.
papers.ideas_for_us: Same group and EEG platform as Selte 2026; a hint that the Wisconsin/WashU overnight hd-EEG pool is large. Context.

papers.title: Sleep homeostasis has circaseptan and circatrigintan cycles over year-long timescales
papers.authors: Vashin V, Magana-Tellez O, Ahrens E, Mosher JC, Lacuey N, Tallavajhula S, Schiess M, Dabaghian Y, Boly M, Duun-Henriksen J, Lhatoo S
papers.question: How does nightly slow-wave decline vary over a year?
papers.tried: Subscalp EEG allows months of continuous recording.
papers.method_data: Subscalp EEG in 20 healthy adults for 12-15 months.
papers.key_results: SWA slope was negative in all subjects; about 7-day and 28-day rhythms appeared in most. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Small; device-specific.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context.

papers.title: White-matter disconnection shapes distributed cortical spectral dynamics after stroke
papers.authors: Mazzonetto I, Celli M, Pini L, et al.
papers.question: Does post-stroke slow-wave activity spread to disconnected but intact cortex?
papers.tried: Slow waves follow structural disconnection (connectional diaschisis).
papers.method_data: 128-channel source EEG with disconnection mapping in 49 acute stroke patients and 20 controls.
papers.key_results: Disconnected regions showed perilesional-like changes: more delta/theta and steeper aperiodic slopes, correlated with severity. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Awake, conscious patients.
papers.ideas_for_us: The aperiodic exponent steepens with disconnection in conscious people, one more reason the exponent is a confound to control, not a consciousness marker. Ledger: large activity changes with consciousness intact (C42-type).

papers.title: Advanced meditation stabilizes cortical dynamics through inhibitory gain control linked to absorptive depth
papers.authors: Panda R, Kumar G, Núñez P, Subramaniam B, Bhandare K, Malipeddi S, Major G, Gosseries O, Laureys S, Tewarie P
papers.question: What stabilises absorptive meditative states?
papers.tried: Corticothalamic gain changes stabilise fast cortical dynamics.
papers.method_data: 18 long-term Rajyoga meditators, EEG rest vs meditation, corticothalamic model fits.
papers.key_results: Meditation raised beta1, beta2 and gamma power with no change in delta, theta or alpha, lowered beta non-stationarity, and fitted stronger cortical inhibitory gain. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Small.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context.

papers.title: Spatial spectral narrowing in the corticothalamic neural field model across consciousness states
papers.authors: Sarker RC, Hye MA
papers.question: Does the corticothalamic model predict a spatial signature of consciousness states?
papers.tried: Analyse the model's spatial noise spectrum across fitted states.
papers.method_data: Robinson model parameters for wake, eMCS, MCS, N3 and UWS.
papers.key_results: Spatial spectral centroid fell by 48% from wake to UWS; no Turing instability in any state. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Model only; offers predictions, not data.
papers.ideas_for_us: A testable prediction on high-density data: spatial-frequency content should narrow from wake to N3. Could be scored as one more state-axis measure on Sleep-EDF/BOAS; not an experience marker.

papers.title: A whole-brain dynamical framework linking resting-state activity to TMS-evoked responses
papers.authors: Veronese A, Momi D, Sarasso S, Corbetta M, Allegra M, Suweis S
papers.question: Can resting EEG predict TMS-evoked responses through a fitted whole-brain model?
papers.tried: Closed-form cross-spectra fit resting EEG; site-specific effective connectivity predicts TEPs.
papers.method_data: Analytic whole-brain model; resting and TMS-EEG.
papers.key_results: The model predicted the spatiotemporal structure of TEPs in unseen trials; group templates captured early site-specific propagation. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Abstract only.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context: another resting-to-perturbation bridge, like Maschke 2024 and Newman 2026.

papers.title: Lack of vision shifts occipital dynamics toward a frontal-like regime and enhances top-down connectivity
papers.authors: Hassan G, Cuntis ID, Gaglioti G, et al.
papers.question: Does blindness retune the intrinsic dynamics of occipital cortex?
papers.tried: TMS-EEG should show occipital responses becoming frontal-like.
papers.method_data: TMS-EEG of frontal and occipital cortex in 16 blind and 16 sighted adults.
papers.key_results: Blind participants had faster, lower-amplitude occipital TEPs resembling frontal ones, and stronger frontal-to-occipital connectivity. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Small.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context.

papers.title: The neural correlates of consciousness: a systematic review and meta-analysis of the visual awareness negativity and P3b
papers.authors: Hutchinson BT, Pustejovsky JE, Bandara K, McGovern H, Cox J, Voce A, Pitts M, Slagter HA
papers.question: Are the VAN and P3b necessary and sufficient markers of visual awareness?
papers.tried: A registered-report meta-analysis of seen and unseen effects with quality and bias moderators.
papers.method_data: 117 studies, 547 seen effect sizes (322 VAN, 225 P3b) and 89 unseen effect sizes.
papers.key_results: VAN standardized mean difference 0.37 (95% CI 0.32-0.43); P3b 0.49 (0.41-0.57). P3b was not reliably present when stimuli were task-irrelevant (-0.12, -0.47 to 0.23), so it is not necessary; the VAN appeared even without awareness, so it is not sufficient. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Abstract only; moderator results not read.
papers.ideas_for_us: Settles two ledger rows: P3b as a report/task marker (C28 line) and VAN as not sufficient. Our GNWT extension (T4) and any Stockart reanalysis should use these effect sizes as priors.

papers.title: Have grand theories of consciousness earned their keep?
papers.authors: Owen AM, Goodale MA
papers.question: Have overarching theories driven the field's real advances?
papers.tried: The biggest advances came from rigorous empirical work, not grand theory.
papers.method_data: Perspective.
papers.key_results: Argues future progress may depend on returning to empirical tradition. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Opinion.
papers.ideas_for_us: Supports our results-first, theory-light ordering; useful framing for the #42 write-up if it is a benchmark rather than a theory test.

papers.title: Systematic theory-method dependencies in consciousness research
papers.authors: Overgaard M, Dietz M, Waade PT
papers.question: Does the experimental method predict which theory a study supports?
papers.tried: If theories share an empirical space, method should not predict support.
papers.method_data: Updated ConTraSt database of 518 experiments; Bayesian regression of theory support on methodological features.
papers.key_results: Decisive evidence that methodology predicts whether a study supports, challenges or ignores a theory; theories occupy partly separate methodological niches. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Correlational; database coding.
papers.ideas_for_us: Direct input for the theory disagreement map (#17) and scorecard (#25): weight evidence by method niche, or a theory's 'wins' partly measure which paradigms its proponents run.

papers.title: No support beyond reach: the Measure Centrality Index 2.0 and adversarial comparisons of consciousness theories
papers.authors: Chis-Ciure R
papers.question: How can preregistered adversarial tests stop passes being claimed for a theory's core while failures are pinned on auxiliaries?
papers.tried: The Reach Principle: a pass counts only as deep as the matching failure would have cut; fix attribution before the result.
papers.method_data: Conceptual framework applied to COGITATE's third prediction.
papers.key_results: On COGITATE prediction 3, the target was the posterior-connectivity implementation; the core of both theories stood outside the test, so a pass could have been claimed at any depth. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Conceptual.
papers.ideas_for_us: Add a 'reach' line to our prereg template: for each outcome, what it counts against and what we agree to change. Cheap and it hardens every sealed test.

papers.title: Why testing structural theories requires the unconscious condition
papers.authors: Zheng Z, Rodrigues JPP, Kob L, Matić K
papers.question: Can structure-matching between qualia and neural structure identify the substrate of experience?
papers.tried: Structure-matching assumes the matching structure is conscious-specific; that must be tested with unseen stimuli.
papers.method_data: Review and proposed design.
papers.key_results: Existing evidence suggests relational structure survives absence of awareness, though no study settles it. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Argument.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context for our theory track; the same logic as our spectral-baseline nesting: a correlate must fail when experience is absent.

papers.title: Long-timescale dynamics shape visual conscious awareness
papers.authors: Zheng Z, Trübutschek D, Cai Y, Melloni L
papers.question: How does conscious awareness fluctuate over time across trials?
papers.tried: Subjective reports should carry long autocorrelation not explained by response bias.
papers.method_data: Reanalysis of 20 existing visual awareness datasets (N = 335) of visibility/confidence and accuracy; one reanalysed single-pulse TMS dataset (right DLPFC vs vertex, 0-500 ms).
papers.key_results: Reanalysis of 20 existing datasets (N = 335). Subjective measures fit an exponential decay; in the 14 datasets with known trial durations the characteristic timescales generally exceeded 5 s, with autocorrelation reaching asymptote over about 30-100 s; accuracy fit a slow linear decay. In a reanalysed TMS dataset (right DLPFC vs vertex, single pulses at 0-500 ms), DLPFC stimulation reduced the amplitude of confidence autocorrelation (beta = -0.129, SE = 0.050, P = 0.010) without changing its decay constant (P = 0.323), and had no detectable effect on objective performance (P = 0.735 intercept, P = 0.589 slope).
papers.limits: All data are reanalysed from earlier studies; the TMS evidence is one dataset with a between-subjects site factor. Long autocorrelation in reports may still partly reflect criterion drift, which the authors argue against but cannot rule out.
papers.ideas_for_us: Serial-awakening reports may also be autocorrelated within a night. #42 already has awakening index and time of night as covariates; the previous report could be checked as a nuisance in an exploratory analysis. Used as a post-cutoff item in the theory-ledger leak probe and manipulation check (experiments/theory_leak).

papers.title: Rapid alternation of conscious and suppressed stimulus representations in the primate brain
papers.authors: Hesse JK, Lanfranchi FF, McGrory C, Shi Y, Engel TA, Tsao DY
papers.question: Is there a pure neural signal of conscious perception in face patches?
papers.tried: Binocular flash suppression with Neuropixels across face patches and prefrontal cortex.
papers.method_data: Macaque Neuropixels recordings in IT face patches and PFC.
papers.key_results: During a constant percept the brain alternated about 15 times per second between conscious and suppressed micro-epochs; each epoch allowed reconstruction of the respective image; tuning was amplified in conscious epochs; PFC was qualitatively similar. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Monkeys; report paradigm details not in abstract.
papers.ideas_for_us: A strong content-NCC result for the ledger and the theory scorecard; not directly testable on our open data.

papers.title: Simultaneous recordings link intracranial and scalp correlates of somatosensory awareness in humans
papers.authors: Mikulan E, Zauli FM, Russo S, Mannini F, Del Vecchio M, Albertini D, d'Orio P, Nobili L, Sartori I, Massimini M, Avanzini P, Pigorini A
papers.question: What is the neural source of the scalp N140, the putative somatosensory awareness negativity?
papers.tried: Simultaneous scalp and intracranial recordings should link N140/SAN to insulo-opercular activity.
papers.method_data: Simultaneous high-density scalp EEG and intracranial EEG during median nerve stimulation.
papers.key_results: The N140/SAN is the scalp expression of the insulo-opercular field potential that follows the tonic broadband high-frequency response. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Abstract only.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context: links a scalp awareness marker to a cortical source.

papers.title: Distinct electrophysiological correlates of low- and high-level visual consciousness with minimized post-perceptual processing
papers.authors: Hense A, Peters A, Dellert T, Bruchmann M, Straube T
papers.question: Do ERP correlates of awareness differ for low- and high-level content when task demands are removed?
papers.tried: Inattentional blindness with three awareness levels for one stimulus.
papers.method_data: 85 participants, inattentional blindness, task-irrelevant stimuli.
papers.key_results: Line awareness enhanced an early occipital negativity; face awareness added a right occipitotemporal negativity and later medial posterior positivities. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Single paradigm.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context; fits the VAN meta-analysis.

papers.title: Testing the prevalent consistency assumption of (un)conscious processing through massive feature extraction of inattentional blindness EEG
papers.authors: Leung A, Kawashima Y, Tsuchiya N
papers.question: Do EEG features that detect invisible stimuli keep doing so when the stimuli become visible?
papers.tried: A registered report testing the consistency assumption behind contrastive NCC analysis.
papers.method_data: Over 7,000 time-series features (hctsa-style toolbox) on inattentional blindness EEG; Bayesian tests.
papers.key_results: Pilot results suggest the assumption is likely invalid across many features. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Registered report; final results pending.
papers.ideas_for_us: Massive feature extraction is our Study 3 route. Their toolbox is the parent of catch22, which is in #42's measure list; worth reading their feature-family handling and multiple-comparison control before sealing Study 3 variants.

papers.title: Is it possible to make unconscious inferences? The limits of the influence of unconsciously perceived stimuli on conscious decisions
papers.authors: Remiszewski M, Łacny J, Cwalina F, Masłowska K, Cleeremans A, Binder M
papers.question: How complex a decision can masked stimuli drive?
papers.tried: Unconscious influence should fade as decisions need integration and inference.
papers.method_data: Sandwich masking at three decision complexities.
papers.key_results: Accuracy 58% for simple decisions, 54% for intermediate, not reliably above chance for complex inference. (abstract only)
papers.limits: One paradigm.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context for ledger psychophysics rows.

papers.title: Integrated information theory (IIT) and the testability of the silent neuron predictions
papers.authors: Ponce de Leon S, Yoshimi J
papers.question: Are IIT's silent-brain and disabled-neuron predictions testable?
papers.tried: A mechanism outside the main complex could report while the complex stays silent.
papers.method_data: Conceptual analysis.
papers.key_results: Argues both predictions can in principle be tested, against Bartlett 2022. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Conceptual.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context for the theory scorecard's IIT row.

papers.title: Overcoming essentialism: evaluation of theories of consciousness by the lawful regularities they predict
papers.authors: Bassler M, Pennartz CMA
papers.question: Should theories be judged by their definition of consciousness?
papers.tried: Judge theories by the testable regularities they propose, not their essence claims.
papers.method_data: Conceptual (Popper).
papers.key_results: No consensus definition is needed for progress. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Conceptual.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context; matches our ledger-and-scorecard approach.

papers.title: Pluralism within limits: how to make the idea of multiple NCC kinds useful
papers.authors: Kob L, Marvan T
papers.question: Can several kinds of NCC all be valid?
papers.tried: A two-factor framework with a finite, ordered set of NCC kinds.
papers.method_data: Conceptual.
papers.key_results: Pluralism is viable only with general factors separated from content encoding. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Conceptual.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context.

papers.title: Brainstem theory of consciousness
papers.authors: Devor M, Baron M
papers.question: Does raw experience come from the brainstem rather than cortex?
papers.tried: Pain, which needs no cortex, shows sentience is brainstem-based.
papers.method_data: Review argument.
papers.key_results: Argues cortical lesions remove 'consciousness of' contents while brainstem lesions abolish sentience. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Contested; argument from lesions and pain.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context for ledger subcortical rows.

papers.title: A Rosetta Stone hypothesis for neurophenomenology: mathematical predictions from predictive processing
papers.authors: Da Costa L, Seth AK, Friston K, Ramstead MJD, Sandved-Smith L
papers.question: Can predictive processing link phenomenology, behaviour and neural dynamics mathematically?
papers.tried: If phenomenology is a function of beliefs, specific predictions follow.
papers.method_data: Theory.
papers.key_results: Derives predictions for similarity judgements, metabolic cost, effort and time perception. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Conditional on a strong assumption.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context for INTREPID-related theory work.

papers.title: A multimodal investigation of perceptual awareness in Alzheimer's disease
papers.authors: Huntley J, Barnett B, Bor D, Mancuso M, Mediano PAM, Naci L, Fleming S, et al.
papers.question: Do EEG and fMRI awareness signatures persist as Alzheimer's progresses?
papers.tried: VAN, late positivity and frontoparietal activation should decline with severity.
papers.method_data: Visual masking EEG and movie fMRI in controls, mild-moderate and severe AD.
papers.key_results: VAN and late positivity and frontoparietal activation were reduced in mild-moderate AD; limited evidence in severe AD. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Task insensitivity in severe AD.
