papers.title: Low-intensity focused ultrasound pulsation along the anterior-posterior thalamic axis differentially modulates the latency of reporting conscious visual experience
papers.authors: Jang H, Liu J, Hudetz AG, Huang Z
papers.question: Does thalamic focused ultrasound change visual categorisation or the report that follows?
papers.tried: Target and duty cycle should affect report latency specifically.
papers.method_data: 60 adults randomised to two duty cycles, four left thalamic targets, acoustic simulations.
papers.key_results: Target-by-duty-cycle interaction for report latency, not categorisation; at the ventroposterior target report latency was 55.9 ms longer under the higher duty cycle. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Latency, not awareness itself.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context.

papers.title: Verbalizable representations form a global workspace in language models
papers.authors: Gurnee W, Sofroniew N, Pearce A, Piotrowski M, Kauvar I, Chen R, Soligo A, Bogdan P, et al.
papers.question: Do language models have a functional analogue of conscious access?
papers.tried: A 'Jacobian lens' finds what a model is poised to verbalise; this J-space should show workspace properties.
papers.method_data: Interpretability study of large language models.
papers.key_results: J-space content can be reported, summoned, held, used for silent reasoning and passed to downstream computation; it is coherent only in a middle band of layers, holds tens of concepts and is broadcast more widely than other representations. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Functional analogy only; says nothing about experience.
papers.ideas_for_us: A concrete, testable workspace signature in AI that maps onto the access side of GNWT; relevant if the AI topic page compares indicators. Follow-ups test it in looped transformers and Mamba (Wang & Reid 2026).

papers.title: Looped transformers under the Jacobian lens: does the global workspace survive recurrence?
papers.authors: Wang W, Reid F
papers.question: Does the workspace analogue appear when depth comes from recurrence?
papers.tried: Extend the Jacobian lens to looped and depth-recurrent models.
papers.method_data: Ouro-2.6B and Huginn-0125 vs Qwen3.6-27B.
papers.key_results: A workspace forms in the iterated part of each architecture, but recurrence changes how it can be read and written. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Abstract only.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context; recurrence matters to RPT and IIT-style claims about AI.

papers.title: From cacophony to hierarchy: a principled framework for assessing AI consciousness
papers.authors: Chandaria S, Muñoz Morán A, Rosas F, Seth A, Shevlin H, Hutter M, Graepel T, Bales A, et al.
papers.question: How can competing theories be combined into one assessment of AI consciousness?
papers.tried: A five-level hierarchy of functional descriptions plus a Bayesian credence model.
papers.method_data: Framework with indicators at each level, applied to current LLMs.
papers.key_results: Verdicts for current LLMs ranged from below 0.01 to about 0.8 depending on stipulated credences. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Outcome driven by priors, as the authors show.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context for the AI topic.

papers.title: Same behavior, different mechanism: what finite experiments can certify about integrated information
papers.authors: Wu L, He D
papers.question: When is integrated information identifiable and certifiable from finite, partial experiments?
papers.tried: Test phi on small stochastic networks with known ground truth.
papers.method_data: Four- and five-unit stochastic networks; partial recordings and interventions.
papers.key_results: A recurrent and a feed-forward network with identical input-output laws carried 0.28 and 0 bits, separable from internal recordings in 4-53 trials. Omitted units imposed precision floors of 0.30-1.02 bits; tiny mechanism changes crossing an edge shifted phi by 25-100% at 99% of edges found. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Tiny networks.
papers.ideas_for_us: Directly relevant to our phi_proxy recovery test: phi is discontinuous in the mechanism, so any proxy recovery test should report how often near-identical networks give very different phi.

papers.title: Existence of an infinite family of substrates satisfying all the postulates of integrated information theory, exclusion included, with arbitrarily large integrated information
papers.authors: Mayeux A
papers.question: Can simple substrates have arbitrarily large integrated information?
papers.tried: A constructive proof.
papers.method_data: Cycles of XOR units.
papers.key_results: Exhibits cycles that are complexes in every state with phi growing as two to a power quadratic in the number of units. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Mathematical.
papers.ideas_for_us: An 'unfolding'-style challenge to IIT for the scorecard; also a stress case for phi_proxy.

papers.title: System-level nonequivalence between integrated information and expected free energy in noisy permutation networks
papers.authors: Tanabe K
papers.question: Does a network's predictive free energy determine its integrated information?
papers.tried: Build networks with identical predictions but different causal wiring.
papers.method_data: Noisy binary permutation networks; exact IIT calculations.
papers.key_results: Architectures with identical one-step predictions and expected free energy had zero (multicycle) or positive (single cycle) system phi; maximum phi approaches one ibit for large n. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Formal.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context for INTREPID-related scorecard rows.

papers.title: A cross-entropy audit (CEA) for consciousness tests moved from brain to large language model
papers.authors: van Rooyen P
papers.question: How often is a brain consciousness test wrong when moved to an LLM?
papers.tried: Score competing models on held-out trials in nats per trial; plant known truth.
papers.method_data: Method proposal with simulations.
papers.key_results: Proposes a transfer audit; no method reviewed measured transfer error rates. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Single author; method proposal.
papers.ideas_for_us: Its held-out log-score idea matches how we compare theories; context.

papers.title: Adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness
papers.authors: Cogitate Consortium (Ferrante, Gorska-Klimowska, Henin, Hirschhorn, Khalaf, Lepauvre, Liu, Richter, Vidal and others)
papers.question: The first big head-to-head test of two theories of consciousness found that each got some predictions right and each got key claims wrong.
papers.method_data: n = 256 (fMRI 120, MEG 102, iEEG 34), suprathreshold faces, objects, letters and false fonts shown for 0.5, 1.0 or 1.5 s, task-relevant and task-irrelevant. Content information found in visual, ventrotemporal and inferior frontal cortex; sustained responses in occipital and lateral temporal cortex tracked duration; content-specific synchronisation between frontal and early visual areas. IIT challenged by no sustained posterior synchronisation; GNWT challenged by general lack of offset ignition and limited prefrontal representation of some conscious dimensions. Preregistration: osf.io/92tbg. Data CC BY 4.0, account needed for download.
papers.key_results: Two rival theories agreed in advance what results would count against them. Then 256 people looked at pictures while their brains were scanned in three different ways. Neither theory won. One theory said the back of the brain should stay in sync for as long as a picture is seen; it did not. The other said the front of the brain should flare up when a picture disappears; mostly it did not.
papers.ideas_for_us: The data is public (Experiment 1: MEG, fMRI, iEEG), so it is the first place we test whether the published conclusions survive other reasonable analyses. Note the paper's iEEG n is 34; the plan said 38.

papers.title: Integrated information and predictive processing theories of consciousness: an adversarial collaborative review (INTREPID)
papers.authors: Corcoran AW, Haun AM, Dorman R, Tononi G, Friston KJ, Pennartz CMA, TWCF INTREPID Consortium
papers.question: The second big adversarial collaboration has published its plan: IIT against two predictive-brain theories. No results yet.
papers.method_data: Compares IIT, neurorepresentationalism (Pennartz) and active inference (Friston): target phenomena, explanatory styles, methods. Lists key hypotheses for multi-site experiments and what would support or challenge each theory, and proposes formally combining results across experiments and replications into a quantitative measure of evidential support per theory. Preprint arXiv:2509.00555 (v1 Aug 2025, v3 May 2026). Online 14 May 2026, issue Aug 2026.
papers.key_results: Three teams with rival theories wrote down, together, which experiments would tell their ideas apart and what each result would mean. The experiments run across several labs. This paper is the agreed plan and a comparison of the theories, not the results.
papers.ideas_for_us: If its data appears after we seal our predictions, it is a clean prospective test. Its evidence-pooling idea is a model for our own log-score comparison of theories.

papers.title: Testing the spatiotemporal predictions of global neuronal workspace theory and integrated information theory
papers.authors: Bandara KH, Rowe EG, Garrido MI
papers.question: Do GNWT's phasic prefrontal ignition (onset and offset) and IIT's sustained posterior feedback show up in directed connectivity of the COGITATE MEG data?
papers.tried: Dynamic causal models with and without each theory's key connections, compared by Bayesian model reduction in expanding time windows.
papers.method_data: COGITATE MEG, task-irrelevant faces (100 recruited, 98 analysed), discovery (N = 48) and validation (N = 52) batches; DCM of prefrontal, fusiform and V1 nodes in expanding windows after onset and offset; post-hoc face-vs-object specificity check. Not peer reviewed.
papers.key_results: Dynamic causal modelling of the MEG data (100 recruited, 98 analysed) split into a discovery batch (N = 48) and a validation batch (N = 52), with expanding time windows. Removing prefrontal-to-fusiform feedback was strongly penalised (posterior probability > 0.95) in the 300-500 ms window after onset and, at offset, from the 400 ms window, in both batches. Fusiform-to-V1 feedback was needed (pp > 0.95) in only 2 of 8 non-successive windows in discovery and was not sustained in validation; intrinsic fusiform gain was needed in every window in validation but dipped at 600 ms in discovery (ending at pp about 0.78). A face-versus-object network check did not reach strong evidence for face selectivity in any window. Unlike the original COGITATE analysis, this finds prefrontal feedback at offset as well as onset.
papers.limits: One reanalysis with many modelling choices on data whose original analysis found no offset ignition; the failed content-specificity check means the network may not be face-specific, which weakens the posterior (sustained) tests most. Not peer reviewed.
papers.ideas_for_us: This is the 'July 2026 reanalysis' the plan could not name. It goes into our multiverse on COGITATE (task #11) as one of the analysis paths, and shows why we hash the analysis set first. Used as a post-cutoff item in the theory-ledger leak probe and manipulation check (experiments/theory_leak).

papers.title: A data-driven approach to identifying and evaluating connectivity-based neural correlates of conscious visual perception
papers.authors: Bryant AG, Whyte CJ
papers.question: Testing 246 ways of measuring brain connectivity on the COGITATE data gives tentative support to the workspace theory.
papers.method_data: COGITATE MEG, 94 of 100 downloaded participants with anatomy for source localisation. 246 functional connectivity measures between IIT- and GNWT-predicted regions; barycenter-based measures decoded stimuli best and generalised across regions. Neural mass models: GNWT with delayed ignition, IIT with synchronous sensory dynamics; both captured the observed patterns. Conclusion: tentative support for GNWT, because ignition appeared regardless of task demands. A correction was issued (niag071).
papers.key_results: Rather than pick one connectivity measure, the authors tried 246 of them on the same public recordings, found the family that best tells pictures apart, and then built small brain models of each theory to see which reproduced it. Both models fit; the authors lean slightly towards the workspace theory.
papers.ideas_for_us: A second independent reanalysis of the same data, from a different angle. Its 246-measure sweep is a template for our pre-registered multiverse; we would hash the measure list first.

papers.title: A dream EEG and mentation database (DREAM)
papers.authors: Wong W, Herzog R, Andrade KC, Andrillon T and others; senior author Tsuchiya N
papers.question: Twenty sleep studies pooled their brain recordings with what people said they were dreaming when woken up: 505 people, 2,643 awakenings.
papers.method_data: Initial release: 20 datasets, 505 participants, 2,643 awakenings; each has sleep M/EEG (>= 20 s, >= 100 Hz, >= 2 electrodes) up to waking plus a standardised report class. Experience vs no experience decoded from EEG over 200 random train-test splits against a label-shuffled null: NREM best with spectral power features (mean AUC 0.586, 5th-95th percentile 0.505-0.608); REM best with catch22 features (mean AUC 0.700, 0.663-0.731). Six datasets used for these analyses. Registry open (doi:10.26180/22133105); dataset packages either open access or by request from the contributor. Main text does not say whether splits held out whole subjects.
papers.key_results: When you wake someone in the night and ask what was going through their mind, sometimes they report a dream and sometimes nothing. Single labs could only collect a few hundred of these. This database pools them, so we can ask, with far more data, whether brain signals before waking predict a dream report.
papers.ideas_for_us: The key resource for our dream vs no-dream test (task #6). Their AUCs are the bar to beat, but we split by subject and lab, so our numbers may come out lower.

papers.title: A repeated awakening study exploring the capacity of complexity measures to capture dreaming during propofol sedation
papers.authors: Bajwa IJ, Nilsen AS, Skukies R, Aamodt A, Ernst G, Storm JF, Juel BE
papers.question: Brain complexity dropped under sedation, but did not differ between people who said they had been dreaming and people who said they had not.
papers.method_data: 20 healthy participants, propofol, resting EEG and TMS-EEG (PCIst) plus single-channel LZc. 52 attempted awakenings: 24 experience, 5 no experience, 23 unarousable or uninformative. Both measures fell from wake to sedation; no evidence of a difference between experience and no-experience awakenings within sedation (linear mixed models). Data: OpenNeuro ds005620 v1.0.0, CC0, 21 subjects, 83.0 GB in full (OpenNeuro metadata).
papers.key_results: Twenty volunteers were sedated and woken several times to ask whether they had experienced anything. Complexity measures fell with sedation as expected. But they did not tell 'I was dreaming' from 'nothing' within sedation. Only 5 wakings gave a clear 'nothing', so the test could only have caught a large difference.
papers.ideas_for_us: One of our L2 datasets. The full set is far over our 1.5 GB budget; we fetch only the pre-awakening sedation files per subject. The 5 no-experience awakenings make it weak alone for dream vs no-dream; pool with DREAM.

papers.title: The role of etiology in the identification of clinical markers of consciousness: comparing EEG alpha power, complexity, and spectral exponent
papers.authors: Maschke C, Belloli L, Manasova D, Sitt JD, Blain-Moraes S
papers.question: In 303 unresponsive patients, a popular complexity measure mostly repeated what the slope of the EEG spectrum already showed; once corrected for that, its diagnostic value vanished.
papers.method_data: 303 unresponsive patients. Shuffle-normalised LZC correlated with the 1-40 Hz spectral exponent at r(197) = 0.86; phase-normalising (surrogates with matched spectrum) reduced this to r(197) = 0.24, and all LZC diagnostic effects vanished; partialling out the exponent did the same. Alpha power had more diagnostic value in anoxic patients; spectral slope only in non-anoxic patients. Code: github.com/BIAPT/Markers.
papers.key_results: A brain 'complexity' score is often used as a sign of consciousness. Here it moved almost in lockstep with a much simpler property of the signal, how fast power falls off with frequency. When the authors compared each recording with scrambled copies that keep that property, the complexity score stopped telling patients apart. Which marker worked also depended on the cause of brain injury.
papers.ideas_for_us: The direct source for our surrogate gate (task #8) and the LZ vs slope test (task #4). It is the PMC12448740 paper the plan cites. We also stratify by aetiology wherever patient data allow.

papers.title: Critical dynamics in spontaneous EEG predict perturbational complexity in disorders of consciousness with measurable evoked responses
papers.authors: Newman D, Maschke C, O'Byrne J, Colombo MA, Comanducci A, Casarotto S, Citerio G, Rosanova M, Massimini M, Jerbi K, Blain-Moraes S
papers.question: Resting brain signals could stand in for the stimulation-based consciousness index in some brain-injured patients, but not across all of them.
papers.method_data: 26 patients (vascular, traumatic, anoxic). Multivariate criticality features did not generalise PCImax prediction across the full cohort; they did when restricted to non-anoxic patients and to patients with non-zero PCImax. Extends Maschke et al. 2024 (anaesthesia) to brain injury. Not peer reviewed.
papers.key_results: The best-tested consciousness index needs a magnetic pulse to the head. This team asked whether ordinary resting EEG can predict it in 26 brain-injured patients. It could not across the whole group, only in patients whose injury was not from lack of oxygen and in those with a measurable response.
papers.ideas_for_us: Tempers the 2024 claim that resting EEG can replace PCI. Our out-of-sample test of that claim should report results by aetiology.

papers.title: Convergent transcriptomic and connectomic controllers of information integration and its anaesthetic breakdown across mammalian brains
papers.authors: Luppi AI, Uhrig L, Tasserie J, Mediano PAM, Rosas FE and others; senior author Stamatakis EA
papers.question: Across humans, monkeys, marmosets and mice, anaesthetics break down the brain's integration of information, and waking a monkey with deep-brain stimulation brings it back.
papers.method_data: fMRI with anaesthesia in humans, macaques, marmosets and mice. Breakdown of integrated information is a convergent effect of diverse anaesthetics; dynamics become harder to control; both reversed by thalamic DBS-induced awakening in macaque. Regional breakdown follows PVALB expression topography; species-specific computational models.
papers.key_results: Brain scans under anaesthesia in four species show the same thing: information stops being combined across the brain. In monkeys, stimulating the thalamus reawakened them and restored it. This points the opposite way from a 2024 rat EEG study where an integration estimate went up under anaesthesia.
papers.ideas_for_us: Shows that whether a Phi-like proxy rises or falls under anaesthesia depends on the modality and the estimator. Our known-Phi network test (task #9) must check each proxy before we trust its direction.

papers.title: Identifying indicators of consciousness in AI systems
papers.authors: Butlin P, Long R, Bayne T, Bengio Y, Birch J, Chalmers D and others (20 authors)
papers.question: A method for judging whether an AI could be conscious by checking its inner workings against what theories of consciousness require, not by what it says.
papers.method_data: Four guidelines for deriving indicators, e.g. indicators should target the central explanatory posits of a theory; illustrated with the indicator list from the 2023 report (arXiv:2308.08708, 19 authors, which drew on recurrent processing, global workspace, higher-order, predictive processing and attention schema theories and concluded no current AI systems are conscious but saw no obvious technical barriers to meeting the indicators). Issue June 2026 (vol 30, issue 6).
papers.key_results: Instead of asking a chatbot whether it feels anything, the authors take the core requirements of several brain theories and check whether an AI system's internal machinery meets them. This builds on their 2023 report, which concluded that no current AI system was a strong candidate.
papers.ideas_for_us: The rubric for our AI stress tests: we use it to find where theories disagree or give absurd answers, never as a verdict on AI and never scoring an AI's self-report.

papers.title: Electrophysiological effects of psilocybin co-administered with midazolam
papers.authors: Sutherland M, Nicholas C, Lennertz R, Wenthur C and others
papers.question: With a sedative given alongside psilocybin, brain-signal complexity still rose as the psychedelic effects came on.
papers.method_data: Oral psilocybin 25 mg plus IV midazolam, high-density EEG. At 15-30 min (midazolam at target, psilocybin likely not): higher beta power, lower spectral exponent. Over the next six hours: higher normalised LZC and spectral exponent, lower broadband power. OAA/S sedation scores improved model fits for alpha power; ASC items improved fits for LZCn and spectral exponent. Small open-label pilot. Preprint bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.07.25.666887.
papers.key_results: Psilocybin was given together with a sedative that blunts memory. Early on, when mainly the sedative was acting, the EEG looked sedated. As the psychedelic took hold over six hours, complexity rose and power fell, and these changes tracked people's ratings of altered experience better than ratings of sedation.
papers.ideas_for_us: A case where complexity and the spectral exponent move together under a drug that changes experience. Our test asks whether complexity adds anything once the exponent is known.

papers.title: Critical dynamics in spontaneous EEG predict anesthetic-induced loss of consciousness and perturbational complexity
papers.authors: Maschke C, O'Byrne J, Colombo MA, Boly M, Gosseries O, Laureys S, Rosanova M, Jerbi K, Blain-Moraes S
papers.question: In 15 healthy adults under three anaesthetics, resting EEG predicted the stimulation-based consciousness index closely.
papers.method_data: 15 healthy adults (propofol 5, xenon 5, ketamine 5), data from earlier studies. Avalanche criticality, chaoticity and related metrics; unconsciousness moved away from criticality and the edge of chaos. Ridge regression on 16 features predicted PCImax; leave-one-subject-out (15 folds) mean absolute error 0.065 (+/- 0.042); a 0.35 threshold separated conscious and unconscious states for true and predicted PCImax.
papers.key_results: Volunteers were put under with propofol, xenon or ketamine; all stopped responding, but only the ketamine group reported vivid dreams afterwards. Measures of how close the resting brain sits to a 'critical' tipping point separated the dreaming group from the others, and predicted each person's score on the magnetic-pulse test.
papers.ideas_for_us: If true, the best-validated measure could be tested on many more open datasets. Caution: 15 subjects, 5 per drug, and the same cohort as Colombo 2019 and Sarasso 2015, so these are not independent replications. We test it out of sample.

papers.title: Exploring effects of anesthesia on complexity, differentiation, and integrated information in rat EEG
papers.authors: Nilsen AS, Arena A, Storm JF
papers.question: In rats, integrated-information estimates from spontaneous EEG went up under anaesthesia, opposite to the stimulation-based index.
papers.method_data: Rats under propofol, sevoflurane and ketamine. PCI (electrical stimulation), LZ and geometric integrated information (PhiG) best separated wake from propofol and sevoflurane. PCI was anti-correlated with spontaneous integrated-information measures, which generally increased under propofol and sevoflurane. Authors suggest perturbation-based and spontaneous measures may be complementary.
papers.key_results: The researchers compared a stimulation-based complexity score with several scores computed from ordinary EEG in rats under three anaesthetics. Some scores worked well. But the estimates of 'integrated information', the quantity at the heart of one major theory, generally rose under propofol and sevoflurane, the reverse of what that theory expects.
papers.ideas_for_us: A warning that Phi proxies may not track what IIT says Phi tracks. Our known-Phi network test checks this before any proxy touches brain data.

papers.title: The integrated information theory of consciousness as pseudoscience
papers.authors: IIT-Concerned, Fleming SM, Frith CD and others
papers.venue: PsyArXiv (open letter); follow-up in Nature Neuroscience 28, 689-693 (2025)
papers.question: A group of researchers called IIT pseudoscience, which set off a public dispute over what counts as a test of a theory of consciousness.
papers.method_data: Letter posted 16 Sep 2023 on PsyArXiv. Follow-up: IIT-Concerned et al., 'What makes a theory of consciousness unscientific?', Nature Neuroscience 28, 689-693, doi:10.1038/s41593-025-01881-x (104 author entries in Crossref, including the collective name). We did not verify the number of signatories on the 2023 letter.
papers.key_results: After press coverage called IIT a leading, tested theory, researchers wrote an open letter objecting. In 2025 a follow-up in Nature Neuroscience argued the theory's core claims cannot be tested even in principle. The row is about what a fair test of a theory of consciousness looks like.
papers.ideas_for_us: It is why we judge every theory only by predictions sealed in advance.

papers.title: Integrated information theory (IIT) 4.0: formulating the properties of phenomenal existence in physical terms
papers.authors: Albantakis L, Barbosa L, Findlay G, Grasso M, Haun AM and others; senior author Tononi G
papers.question: The current formal version of integrated information theory.
papers.method_data: Axioms to postulates to mathematical expressions; a unique measure of intrinsic information consistent with the postulates; explicit treatment of causal relations; a system's unfolded cause-effect structure accounts for the quality of experience.
papers.key_results: IIT starts from what experience is like and works out what a physical system must be like to have it, then puts that in mathematics. In principle the maths says whether any system is conscious and how. In practice it cannot be computed for a brain, so only rough stand-ins can be tested.
papers.ideas_for_us: The reference for the IIT row on our scoreboard and for which toy networks have exactly computable Phi in our planted-answer tests.

papers.title: The neural correlates of dreaming
papers.authors: Siclari F, Baird B, Perogamvros L, Bernardi G, LaRocque JJ, Riedner B, Boly M, Postle BR, Tononi G
papers.question: Less slow activity at the back of the brain marked dreaming in both kinds of sleep, and could predict a dream report in real time.
papers.method_data: High-density EEG, serial awakenings. Dream reports in NREM and REM associated with local decreases in low-frequency activity in posterior cortex; high-frequency activity there correlated with specific dream contents; real-time monitoring predicted dream vs no-dream reports in NREM.
papers.key_results: People were woken many times a night and asked if they had been dreaming. In both dreaming-heavy and dreaming-light stages of sleep, a dream report followed a drop in slow brain waves over a 'hot zone' at the back of the head. Watching that zone live predicted whether the sleeper would report a dream.
papers.ideas_for_us: The sharpest within-stage test of a measure against report. The DREAM database (2025) lets us test whether it replicates across labs.

papers.title: Stratification of unresponsive patients by an independently validated index of brain complexity
papers.authors: Casarotto S, Comanducci A, Rosanova M and others; senior author Massimini M
papers.question: A cutoff on the stimulation-based complexity index, set in people who could report, separated conscious from unconscious perfectly and flagged some 'vegetative' patients as possibly conscious.
papers.method_data: Benchmark population 150 (healthy and communicative brain-injured; wake, disconnected consciousness, unconsciousness). Optimal cutoff gave 100% sensitivity and specificity in the benchmark; applied to 38 MCS and 43 VS patients: 94.7% sensitivity for MCS; 9 of 43 VS patients above the cutoff.
papers.key_results: The team first set a threshold using 150 people whose state was known from their own reports. That threshold then caught almost all minimally conscious patients, and showed 9 of 43 patients judged vegetative with scores like conscious people.
papers.ideas_for_us: The strongest published L2 result. No open TMS-EEG set of this kind exists, which is the biggest data gap in our plan.

papers.title: A theoretically based index of consciousness independent of sensory processing and behavior (PCI)
papers.authors: Casali AG, Gosseries O, Rosanova M, Boly M, Sarasso S and others; senior author Massimini M
papers.question: The paper that introduced the perturbational complexity index: tap the brain with a magnetic pulse and measure how complex the echo is.
papers.method_data: TMS-evoked EEG responses compressed (Lempel-Ziv) after source modelling and binarisation. Tested in wake, dreaming, NREM sleep, midazolam, xenon and propofol sedation, and in vegetative, minimally conscious and locked-in patients; discriminated level of consciousness in single individuals.
papers.key_results: If a brain is both well connected and varied, a magnetic pulse should set off a rich, hard-to-compress pattern of activity. The score built on that idea separated wake from deep sleep and anaesthesia in single people, and tracked recovery in patients emerging from coma.
papers.ideas_for_us: The measure every spontaneous-EEG candidate is judged against.

papers.title: Consciousness and complexity during unresponsiveness induced by propofol, xenon, and ketamine
papers.authors: Sarasso S, Boly M, Napolitani M and others; senior author Massimini M
papers.question: Under ketamine, people stopped responding but their brain's response to a magnetic pulse stayed wake-like, and afterwards they reported vivid dreams.
papers.method_data: 18 healthy volunteers. Frontal and parietal TMS: propofol gave a local low-complexity slow wave, xenon a global stereotyped low-complexity slow wave, ketamine a wake-like complex pattern. Reports on emergence: none after propofol and xenon; long vivid dreams after ketamine.
papers.key_results: Three anaesthetics all made volunteers unresponsive. After propofol and xenon they remembered nothing. After ketamine they described long, vivid dreams, and during it the brain's response to stimulation stayed complex like in waking. This is the classic case where behaviour and experience come apart.
papers.ideas_for_us: Defines our ketamine dissociation case. The same group's data underlies Colombo 2019 and Maschke 2024, so we need an independent ketamine dataset.

papers.title: Increased spontaneous MEG signal diversity for psychoactive doses of ketamine, LSD and psilocybin
papers.authors: Schartner MM, Carhart-Harris RL, Barrett AB, Seth AK, Muthukumaraswamy SD
papers.question: Psychedelics pushed brain-signal diversity above normal waking levels, the first time such measures went higher than wakefulness.
papers.method_data: Spontaneous MEG; LZ and entropy measures higher for all three drugs, even when controlling for spectral changes; strongest for single-channel LZ (temporal diversity). Selective correlations with phenomenological intensity ratings.
papers.key_results: Complexity scores are usually highest in normal waking. Under psilocybin, ketamine and LSD they went higher still, and some of the rise tracked how intense people said the experience was.
papers.ideas_for_us: Tests whether a measure rises when contents intensify but level does not obviously change. We re-check the spectral control with phase-randomised surrogates.

papers.title: Large scale screening of neural signatures of consciousness in patients in a vegetative or minimally conscious state
papers.authors: Sitt JD, King JR, El Karoui I, Rohaut B, Faugeras F, Gramfort A, Cohen L, Sigman M, Dehaene S, Naccache L
papers.question: Which EEG measures separate vegetative from minimally conscious patients?
papers.tried: Screen many spectral, complexity and connectivity measures at once.
papers.method_data: 181 high-density EEG recordings from DoC patients and controls.
papers.key_results: Theta/alpha power, complexity and wSMI in theta/alpha separated VS from MCS; combined in a classifier they did best.
papers.limits: Single centre at the time; spectral and complexity features were not nested.
papers.ideas_for_us: The source of wSMI and the 'many markers' design that #42 inherits; our nesting rule asks what each adds beyond spectrum.

papers.title: Robust EEG-based cross-site and cross-protocol classification of states of consciousness
papers.authors: Engemann DA, Raimondo F, King JR, Rohaut B, Louppe G, Faugeras F, Annen J, Cassol H, Gosseries O, Fernandez-Slezak D, Laureys S, Naccache L, Dehaene S, Sitt JD
papers.question: Do EEG classifiers of DoC states transfer across sites and protocols?
papers.tried: Random forest on Sitt-style markers, trained in Paris, tested in Liège.
papers.method_data: 327 DoC recordings plus 66 controls; cross-site test.
papers.key_results: Cross-site AUC 0.73-0.78.
papers.limits: Spectral markers carried much of the performance.
papers.ideas_for_us: A benchmark for what held-out DoC classification achieves; the bar Study 2's DoC arm would need to meet.

papers.title: Neural correlates of consciousness: progress and problems
papers.authors: Koch C, Massimini M, Boly M, Tononi G
papers.question: What counts as a neural correlate of consciousness, and where is it?
papers.tried: Define the NCC as the minimal mechanisms sufficient for a percept and separate it from prerequisites and consequences.

papers.title: Cross-Laboratory Validation of EEG Classification of Reported Dream Experience
papers.authors: Bazán Sánchez JE
papers.question: Does the DREAM paper's EEG classifier of reported experience (Figure 5) transfer between laboratories?
papers.tried: Re-run the DREAM Figure 5 workflow (spectral power and catch22 features) and split its accuracy into record-wise, participant-held-out, within-lab and lab-held-out parts, with a lab-prevalence-only baseline and a lab-identity decoder.
papers.method_data: 1,065 reports from the five DREAM collections enumerated by DREAM's released experienceclassification code; NREM spectral power and REM catch22 classifiers.
papers.key_results: Record-wise AUROC 0.569 (NREM spectral) and 0.636 (REM catch22). Participant-held-out pooled 0.534 and 0.629. Within the same lab (site-conditioned) 0.498 and 0.498. Lab-held-out macro AUROC 0.493 and 0.470. A baseline that knows only each lab's report prevalence reaches 0.564 and 0.687 pooled. Lab identity is decoded from the same EEG features at macro AUROC 0.808-0.953. Conclusion: pooled discriminability is real but no common EEG marker transports between labs.
papers.limits: Numbers from the abstract as read in the full text by the coordinator in a browser; our automated fetch was blocked by ResearchGate (403) and not worked around. Generic features (spectra, catch22), NREM pooled across stages as in DREAM Figure 5; no hypothesis-driven consciousness markers, no within-person N2-only analysis reported in the abstract. Single author, not peer reviewed.
papers.ideas_for_us: Pre-empts #42's cross-lab spectral test and its planned headline contrast (pooled AUC driven by lab and between-person differences). Together with the Michalak within-person null (amendment 5) and our Tononi delta result, the spectral arm of #42 is no longer new. Anything left is within-person, N2-only, cross-lab tests of hypothesis-driven markers, with bounds: atlas material.

papers.limits: Condition-averaged ERPs: no single-trial or fixed-SOA seen vs unseen test. OSF data has no licence stated; analysed locally with derived statistics only (coordinator decision 2026-11-24), and the corresponding author was asked about reuse terms.
papers.ideas_for_us: Primary dataset for the fixed-SOA seen vs unseen kill test (experiments/cohen_fixed_soa) and the no-report bifurcation test (experiments/bifurcation).

papers.title: Bifurcation dynamics in a shared network beyond sensory areas characterize conscious auditory perception independently of report
papers.authors: Boyer J, Beraud N, Béranger B, Hardy T, Türker B, Gouyette H, Lopez-Persem A, Sergent C
papers.question: Which brain networks produce all-or-none bifurcation dynamics in conscious perception, with and without a task?
papers.tried: fMRI with near-threshold sounds in task and no-task contexts; single-trial modelling of bifurcation.
papers.method_data: fMRI; sample size not in the abstract.
papers.key_results: Intensity modulated broad networks including PFC in both contexts; single-trial models found bifurcation beyond primary sensory cortex and predicted perception trial by trial in both contexts.
papers.limits: Originating lab (Sergent); abstract only; no planted or recovery check stated. Licence CC BY-NC-ND.
papers.ideas_for_us: Narrows the novelty of the bifurcation kill test: the originating lab has now shown no-task bifurcation in EEG (2021) and fMRI. What stays open is an outside, sealed, planted-bounded test across Cohen and Sergent EEG.

papers.title: Identifying neural correlates of auditory perceptual awareness and deviance using a no-report inattentional deafness paradigm
papers.authors: Ellinghorst A, Dellert T, Zhu Y, Straube T, Dykstra AR, Schloßmacher I
papers.question: Can awareness, deviance and task relevance be separated in auditory ERPs?
papers.tried: Multitone masking; three phases with identical tone pairs: naive (unaware), informed (aware), task-relevant.
papers.method_data: EEG ERPs; physically identical target-tone pairs in multitone masks across three fixed-order phases (naive, informed, task-relevant gap judgement); sample size not in the abstract.
papers.key_results: Physically identical target-tone pairs in multitone masks across three phases differing only in instructions: naive (unaware), informed (aware, task-irrelevant), and task-relevant (gap judgement). Awareness gave an auditory awareness negativity and an increased positivity in the P3 window, both larger when task-relevant. Deviants gave a mismatch negativity in all phases (largest when task-relevant), while a significant deviant P3 appeared only in the task-relevant phase. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Abstract only; sample size and effect sizes not in the abstract. Awareness is manipulated between fixed-order phases, so time on task and expectation are confounded with awareness; condition-averaged ERPs.
papers.ideas_for_us: Not a single-trial bifurcation test, so no threat to that study's novelty. Shows AAN and P3 can be dissociated from report in audition. Used as a post-cutoff item in the theory-ledger leak probe and manipulation check (experiments/theory_leak).

papers.title: A dynamic bifurcation mechanism explains cortex-wide neural correlates of conscious access
papers.authors: Klatzmann U, Froudist-Walsh S, Bliss DP, Theodoni P, Mejías JF, Niu M, Rapan L, Palomero-Gallagher N, Sergent C, Dehaene S, Wang XJ
papers.question: What network mechanism produces all-or-none ignition across cortex?
papers.tried: Simulation of a detection task in a connectome-based model of macaque cortex.
papers.method_data: Computational model; receptor predictions checked against in vitro autoradiography.
papers.key_results: A dynamic bifurcation in associative regions produces ignition; an NMDA/AMPA gradient shapes it, with higher NMDA:AMPA ratios predicted in sensory than association areas.
papers.limits: Model only, no human EEG test of single-trial bimodality.
papers.ideas_for_us: The 'cortex-wide bifurcation' paper the coordinator asked about (not by Garnier-Allain). Gives the theory behind the bifurcation kill test; does not pre-empt it.

papers.title: "The self" as shifting coalitions of brain systems in a continuous configuration space
papers.authors: Skipper JI, Blackburne G, Cooper G, Jaglinska M, Jedlovszky K, Kuc J, McAlpine R, Timmermann C
papers.question: Is there a core brain region or network for the self?
papers.tried: Meta-analysis of 912 neuroimaging papers; titles and abstracts clustered into ten forms of self; brain maps per form; held-out prediction of reported regions.
papers.method_data: 912 publications, ten self-related maps (e.g. autobiographical memory, body ownership, interoception).
papers.key_results: No location significant in all ten maps; maps related selectively to aspects of consciousness; graded mixtures of maps predicted held-out papers' regions better than single maps or on/off combinations.
papers.limits: Abstract only. 'No core' rests partly on a failed conjunction across ten maps, an absence-of-evidence inference whose sensitivity is not stated in the abstract. Licence CC BY-NC-ND (no figure reuse).
papers.ideas_for_us: Self and ego are related to consciousness, not the same. Relevant to ego dissolution (psychedelics; Timmermann is an author) and to any self-consciousness study. A planted check of the conjunction null (could a real shared core have been detected?) would fit our null-audit style.

papers.title: An adversarial collaboration protocol for testing contrasting predictions of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theory
papers.authors: Melloni L, Mudrik L, Pitts MA, Bendtz K, Ferrante O, Górska U, Hirschhorn R, Khalaf AF, and others
papers.question: How can GNW and IIT be tested against each other with predictions both sides agree on in advance?
papers.tried: The COGITATE protocol: two experiments with predictions signed off by GNW and IIT proponents. Experiment 1 shows clearly visible stimuli with task relevance varied; experiment 2 hides faces and objects in the background of a demanding video game, so some are missed (inattentional blindness), then replays the same displays with a detection task.
papers.method_data: fMRI, M-EEG and iEEG at several sites. Experiment 2 contrasts seen vs unseen under distraction, and tests whether brain patterns generalise between distracted and attended viewing.
papers.key_results: Protocol only. In experiment 2, GNW predicts conscious content decodable from prefrontal cortex at 300-500 ms, prefrontal-to-category-area synchrony for seen stimuli, no seen/unseen difference before 250 ms, and higher prefrontal pre-stimulus activity before missed stimuli. IIT predicts posterior patterns that stay the same across tasks for seen stimuli and posterior (category area to V1/V2) synchrony.
papers.limits: Frequent awareness probes make the 'unattended' stimuli partly task-relevant, which blurs the inattention manipulation. Experiment 2 results were not public as of 2026-11-21.
papers.ideas_for_us: Basis for our sealed forecasts of experiment 2 (docs/prereg/2026-11-21_cogitate_exp2_forecasts.md, 17 items, scored against each theory as a forecaster).

papers.title: GNW theoretical framework and the "adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness"
papers.authors: Naccache L, Sergent C, Dehaene S, Wang XJ, Farisco M, Changeux JP
papers.question: How do GNW's proponents read the COGITATE experiment 1 results?
papers.tried: A reply by GNW proponents to the COGITATE 2025 results.
papers.method_data: Commentary on published data; no new data.
papers.key_results: They say several core GNW predictions were confirmed (onset ignition, frontal content decoding, frontal-visual synchrony); offset ignition is not a core prediction; and COGITATE experiment 1 could not test GNW's central claim, conscious vs unconscious processing, because every stimulus was clearly visible.
papers.limits: Written by the theory's proponents. The offset-ignition prediction was signed off before the results.
papers.ideas_for_us: Shows why experiment 2 (seen vs unseen) is the test GNW proponents call decisive. Our forecasts take that test as the target.

papers.title: Neural signatures of conscious face perception in an inattentional blindness paradigm
papers.authors: Shafto JP, Pitts MA
papers.question: Which EEG responses track awareness of faces when the faces are irrelevant to the task?
papers.tried: Three-phase inattentional blindness design: faces shown during a demanding task (some people miss them), then the same with awareness, then with the faces task-relevant.
papers.method_data: EEG ERPs; line-drawing faces and matched controls.
papers.key_results: The N170 and the visual awareness negativity (about 260-300 ms) were absent during inattentional blindness and present with awareness. The P3b appeared only when faces were task-relevant, not when they were seen but irrelevant.
papers.limits: Abstract only. Awareness varies between people and phases, not trial by trial.
papers.ideas_for_us: Prior for COGITATE experiment 2: expect posterior seen-vs-unseen differences before 300 ms, which counts against GNW's 'no difference before 250 ms'. Used in our sealed forecasts.

papers.title: Gamma band activity and the P3 reflect post-perceptual processes, not visual awareness
papers.authors: Pitts MA, Padwal J, Fennelly D, Martínez A, Hillyard SA
papers.question: Are induced gamma and the P3 markers of awareness, or of what we do with a stimulus?
papers.tried: EEG experiments that vary awareness and task relevance separately.
papers.method_data: EEG; inattentional blindness paradigm.
papers.key_results: Induced gamma and the P3 were absent for task-irrelevant stimuli whether or not people were aware of them, and present for task-relevant ones.
papers.limits: Abstract only.
papers.ideas_for_us: Prior for COGITATE experiment 2: late and gamma-band differences may track the probe task, not awareness. Used in our sealed forecasts.

papers.title: Visual processing of contour patterns under conditions of inattentional blindness
papers.authors: Pitts MA, Martínez A, Hillyard SA
papers.question: Which ERPs differ for shapes people did or did not notice?
papers.tried: Inattentional blindness for square contour patterns formed by task-irrelevant line segments, across three phases.
papers.method_data: EEG ERPs; more than half the subjects missed the patterns in phase 1.
papers.key_results: Occipital ERPs at 220-260 ms differed for patterns vs random arrays whether or not people were aware; at 300-340 ms occipito-parietal differences appeared only with awareness.
papers.limits: Abstract only. Awareness assessed after blocks, not trial by trial.
papers.ideas_for_us: Some early processing proceeds without awareness, and awareness adds a slightly later posterior response. Prior for our COGITATE experiment 2 forecasts.

papers.title: Towards full-stack functionalist theories of consciousness: Identifying the functional profile
papers.authors: Thorat S, Chopra P
papers.question: If consciousness is something a system does, what does being aware of a thing change about how the system can use it?
papers.tried: They searched the literature for experiments that compare using the same information with and without awareness, and kept only those where the unaware version did not simply carry weaker information (for example, by matching how well people could discriminate the stimulus).
papers.method_data: Literature review with strict inclusion rules: awareness measured or validated, information strength matched or ruled out by design (a reversal), and an outcome that says how the information is used. Sweep code: github.com/Lossfunk/consciousness-sweep.
papers.key_results: Only a few studies pass. Awareness goes with control over attention (Tsushima 2006: faint, invisible motion distracted people more than stronger, visible motion, as if visible distractors can be suppressed) and with knowing when you're right (Persaud 2011: blindsight patient GY was equally accurate in both visual fields, but his bets tracked his accuracy far better in the seeing field, r = .52 vs .30). Simple binding of a feature to a location worked without awareness (Keizer 2015). They then argue a full theory must also explain what experience is like and why people find it mysterious, and use Attention Schema Theory as the worked example of going from one such finding to a buildable architecture.
papers.limits: The profile is thin: metacognition rests mainly on one patient, binding on one paradigm. The binding 'no difference' is a non-significant interaction (8.6 vs 5.8 ms), not shown equivalence, as the authors say. Neural signatures are excluded unless their computation is known.
papers.ideas_for_us: This is the basis of our 'Can AI be conscious?' sub-project: the self-model agents study tries their agenda item 4 (build agents that model their own attention, ablate the model, check the profile). Also: audit the power of the binding null (as in the COGITATE null audit), and seal AST predictions for COGITATE experiment 2.

papers.title: Spectral Slope and Lempel-Ziv Complexity as Robust Markers of Brain States during Sleep and Wakefulness
papers.authors: Höhn C, Hahn MA, Lendner JD, Hoedlmoser K
papers.question: How do the EEG spectral slope and Lempel-Ziv complexity behave across sleep stages and waking tasks, and does the frequency range matter?
papers.tried: They recorded 28 young men over two weeks (three nights and days each) and computed slope and LZ in a broad (1-45 Hz) and a narrow (30-45 Hz) range.
papers.method_data: Within-subject EEG across wake tasks (rest, attention, memory) and sleep stages; FOOOF and robust fits for the slope; LZ after Comsa 2019.
papers.key_results: From wake to N3 the broadband slope steepened and LZ fell. REM was best told apart by the narrowband slope. They write that LZ 'is still strongly influenced by oscillatory activity', and conclude the slope carries more information than LZ.
papers.limits: No test of whether LZ adds anything over a full spectral baseline, and no phase-randomised surrogates. Only men aged 18-25.
papers.ideas_for_us: Prior art for our LZ result. Our finding that LZ is mostly the spectrum in sleep confirms theirs; what we add is the sealed incremental-AUC test and the surrogate gate.

papers.title: Low frequency oscillations drive EEG's complexity changes during wakefulness and sleep
papers.authors: González J, Mateos D, Cavelli M, Mondino A, Pascovich C, Torterolo P, Rubido N
papers.question: Why does EEG complexity drop in slow-wave sleep: is it the oscillations?
papers.tried: They tested how the frequency content of brain signals in freely moving rats shapes complexity estimates across sleep and wake.
papers.method_data: Rat recordings at micro, meso and macro scales across the sleep-wake cycle.
papers.key_results: The low-frequency spectrum (delta, theta, sigma) drives the complexity changes between sleep and wake.
papers.limits: Rats; abstract only read here.
papers.ideas_for_us: Earliest prior art we found for 'complexity in sleep is spectral'. Cite it beside Höhn 2024 whenever we state our LZ result.

papers.title: Neural complexity is a common denominator of human consciousness across diverse regimes of cortical dynamics
papers.authors: Frohlich J, Chiang JN, Mediano PAM, Nespeca M, Saravanapandian V, et al.
papers.question: When brain rhythms and conscious state come apart, which EEG markers still track consciousness?
papers.tried: They used two rare genetic conditions as a testbed: children with Angelman syndrome look sleep-like while awake, and children with Dup15q look wake-like in NREM sleep.
papers.method_data: Regularised logistic classifiers trained on wake vs NREM in Angelman children, using entropy (complexity) or spectral features, then tested on typical children and on Dup15q.
papers.key_results: Entropy-based markers were not capped by spectral ones and beat them.
papers.limits: Children with rare syndromes; abstract only read here.
papers.ideas_for_us: The strongest counter-evidence to our 'complexity is just the spectrum' result. Our result holds for typical sleep EEG; a dissociation testbed like theirs is the right confound control for any marker tournament.

papers.title: Distinct EEG signatures differentiate unconsciousness and disconnection during anaesthesia and sleep
papers.authors: Casey CP, Tanabe S, Farahbakhsh Z, et al.
papers.question: Can EEG tell 'experiencing but cut off from the world' (disconnected) apart from 'no experience at all' (unconscious)?
papers.tried: Volunteers were sedated with dexmedetomidine or propofol, or slept, under high-density EEG, and were woken repeatedly to ask whether they had experienced anything in the previous 20 s.
papers.method_data: Serial awakenings; derivation on dexmedetomidine, validation on sleep and propofol; source-localised SVM classifiers.
papers.key_results: Occipital delta power barely separated the two states (AUC 0.61 for dexmedetomidine, 0.51 for sleep/propofol). Source-localised signatures did well within dexmedetomidine and generalised partly (disconnection AUC 0.74, unconsciousness 0.62).
papers.limits: Small samples; generalisation AUCs are modest.
papers.ideas_for_us: A model for splitting state contrasts by report. ds005620 (propofol with repeated awakenings) could support the same disconnected-vs-unconscious split.

papers.title: Quantifying arousal and awareness in altered states of consciousness using interpretable deep learning
papers.authors: Lee M, Sanz LRD, Barra A, Wolff A, Nieminen JO, Boly M, et al.
papers.question: Can one EEG index separate arousal (being awake) from awareness (having experience)?
papers.tried: They trained an explainable deep network on EEG responses to TMS across sleep, anaesthesia and brain injury, and also tested resting EEG.
papers.method_data: TMS-EEG in sleep (n=6), general anaesthesia (n=16) and severe brain injury (n=34); resting EEG under anaesthesia (n=15) and brain injury (n=34).
papers.key_results: The index tracked both components across physiological, drug and injury states; ketamine anaesthesia and REM sleep came out as low arousal with high awareness.
papers.limits: Small groups per state; abstract only read here.
papers.ideas_for_us: Closest existing cross-state 'one marker everywhere' attempt. Any tournament must beat or explain this, and must report sample sizes per state honestly.

papers.title: How well do neural signatures of resting-state EEG detect consciousness? A large-scale clinical study
papers.authors: Ma X, Qi Y, Xu C, et al.
papers.question: Which of the many proposed EEG signatures of consciousness actually work in a large patient sample?
papers.tried: They computed 380 resting-EEG metrics in 296 people (99 UWS, 129 MCS, 36 emerged from MCS, 32 healthy) and evaluated each with bootstrap resampling.
papers.method_data: Spectral, nonlinear, connectivity and graph measures; bootstrap evaluation.
papers.key_results: Relative alpha and delta power were the most dependable markers of consciousness.
papers.limits: One clinical cohort; DoC only; abstract only read here.
papers.ideas_for_us: A many-marker screen already exists for DoC, and simple spectral power won. Supports our habit of requiring every marker to beat the spectrum.

papers.title: Dynamical structure-function correlations provide robust and generalizable signatures of consciousness in humans
papers.authors: Castro P, Luppi A, Tagliazucchi E, Perl YS, et al.
papers.question: Do whole-brain fMRI dynamics give a signature of unconsciousness that holds across anaesthesia and deep sleep?
papers.tried: They clustered transient functional-connectivity states in resting fMRI across anaesthesia and slow-wave sleep.
papers.method_data: Resting fMRI; dynamic FC clustering; entropy of state transitions.
papers.key_results: Unconsciousness is dominated by one recurrent pattern tied to structural connectivity, with fewer transitions; rich dynamics (entropy) go with consciousness.
papers.limits: fMRI, not EEG; abstract only read here.
papers.ideas_for_us: Cross-state generalisation has been done in fMRI. Our open EEG data cannot copy this, but it sets the bar for 'generalises across states'.

papers.title: Comprehensive profiling of anaesthetised brain dynamics across phylogeny
papers.authors: Luppi AI, Uhrig L, Tasserie J, Shafiei G, et al.
papers.question: Is there a shared dynamical signature of anaesthesia across species?
papers.tried: They extracted over 6,000 time-series features from recordings in wake and anaesthesia in humans, macaques, marmosets, mice, zebrafish and worms.
papers.method_data: Massive feature extraction (hctsa-style) on multi-scale data; deep-brain stimulation in macaques; biophysical modelling.
papers.key_results: Anaesthesia shows a conserved profile: shorter intrinsic timescales and weaker synchrony between regions. Thalamic stimulation reversed it in macaques.
papers.limits: Preprint; abstract only read here.
papers.ideas_for_us: A huge feature screen for anaesthesia already exists. A tournament adds value only through sealing, held-out data and beating the spectrum.

papers.title: On the independence of visual awareness and metacognition: a signal detection theoretic analysis
papers.authors: Jachs B, Blanco MJ, Grantham-Hill S, Soto D
papers.venue: J Exp Psychol Hum Percept Perform
papers.question: Does knowing whether you are right (metacognition) depend on being aware of the stimulus?
papers.tried: People judged the tilt of a masked, near-threshold grating, then reported awareness and confidence on every trial.
papers.method_data: Three experiments; type-1 (perceptual) and type-2 (metacognitive) sensitivity by awareness level. Data are in the Confidence Database.
papers.key_results: Awareness strongly raised perceptual sensitivity but changed metacognitive sensitivity much less.
papers.limits: Small samples; binary awareness; no stimulus manipulation; abstract only read here (paywalled).
papers.ideas_for_us: The single-study version of our planned metacognition test, so its data cannot be reused as new evidence. Our test needs a simulated signal-detection null because rating-defined 'unseen' trials are biased.

papers.title: Visibility Is Not Equivalent to Confidence in a Low Contrast Orientation Discrimination Task
papers.authors: Rausch M, Zehetleitner M
papers.question: Are 'how clearly did you see it' and 'how sure are you' the same report?
papers.tried: Twenty people judged grating orientation at six contrasts and gave both visibility and confidence on continuous scales every trial, in counterbalanced order.
papers.method_data: meta-d_a for each scale by contrast, metacognitive bias, conditional report rates at a 25% cut, Bayesian mixed models. Data are in the Confidence Database (Rausch_2016).
papers.key_results: Confidence tracked accuracy better than visibility (meta-d_a 1.2 vs 0.5). People were often confident without seeing, but hardly ever saw without being confident.
papers.limits: One lab, n=20. It compares the two scales; it does not test whether confidence works better on high-visibility trials.
papers.ideas_for_us: The only open dataset that can test the Persaud-style claim in healthy people with continuous scales. Our power gate decides whether n=20 is enough.

papers.title: Distilling the neural correlates of consciousness
papers.authors: Aru J, Bachmann T, Singer W, Melloni L
papers.question: Does comparing 'seen' with 'unseen' isolate the brain activity of experience itself?
papers.tried: A conceptual analysis of the contrastive method.
papers.method_data: Review.
papers.key_results: The seen-minus-unseen contrast mixes the NCC proper with its prerequisites (what must happen first) and its consequences (what follows, like report).
papers.limits: Conceptual; abstract only read here.
papers.ideas_for_us: Any marker tournament must say whether a marker is a prerequisite, the NCC or a consequence; state markers (sleep, anaesthesia) mostly index prerequisites.

papers.title: No-Report Paradigms: Extracting the True Neural Correlates of Consciousness
papers.authors: Tsuchiya N, Wilke M, Frässle S, Lamme VAF
papers.question: Does asking people to report what they saw contaminate the search for the brain basis of experience?
papers.tried: A review of report-based and no-report designs.
papers.method_data: Review.
papers.key_results: Report requirements have biased NCC research; no-report paradigms try to remove that bias, with their own trade-offs.
papers.limits: Abstract only read here.
papers.ideas_for_us: Background for our closed no-report bifurcation test and for the report confound in any tournament.

papers.title: The No-Report Paradigm: A Revolution in Consciousness Research?
papers.authors: Duman I, Ehmann IS, Gonsalves AR, Gültekin Z, et al.
papers.question: Do no-report paradigms actually deliver report-free NCCs?
papers.tried: They examined published comparisons of report and no-report conditions.
papers.method_data: Critical review.
papers.key_results: Every example they examined allows alternative readings or has method problems; removing the report does not stop people reflecting on what they saw.
papers.limits: Abstract only read here.
papers.ideas_for_us: Caution for any 'controls for report' claim in our studies.

papers.title: The ConTraSt database for analysing and comparing empirical studies of consciousness theories
papers.authors: Yaron I, Melloni L, Pitts M, Mudrik L
papers.question: Does the evidence for each consciousness theory depend on how studies were designed?
papers.tried: They coded 412 experiments interpreted in light of four leading theories.
papers.method_data: Database and meta-research analysis.
papers.key_results: Which theory a study supports can be predicted from its method choices alone, and most studies interpret findings after the fact rather than testing predictions set in advance.
papers.limits: Abstract only read here.
papers.ideas_for_us: The core argument for sealing definitions and scoring rules before data, as any tournament must.

papers.title: A three-component dynamical index of consciousness-related neural organisation
papers.authors: Ugail H, Howard N
papers.question: Can combining several EEG properties into one index track consciousness better than any single feature?
papers.tried: They combined scale-free timing, cross-frequency organisation and metastable synchrony into one index, tested on simulated states and real EEG.
papers.method_data: Generative model of nine EEG-like states plus empirical data (Sleep-EDF, per the coordinator's note).
papers.key_results: They report the composite index separates states better than single features.
papers.limits: Abstract only read here; the empirical test is limited.
papers.ideas_for_us: One of the composite-index claims a tournament would have to include and test against the spectrum.

papers.title: Neural correlates of perceptual consciousness from within: a narrative review of human intracranial research
papers.authors: (see arXiv)
papers.question: What can intracranial recordings tell us about the NCC that scalp methods cannot?
papers.tried: A narrative review of single-neuron and population recordings in humans.
papers.method_data: Review.
papers.key_results: Intracranial data can help separate proper NCCs from other processes, but the problem is not solved; they lay out limits and future paradigms.
papers.limits: Abstract only read here; authors not recorded.
papers.ideas_for_us: Background on the prerequisite/NCC/consequence problem; relevant once COGITATE iEEG access arrives.

papers.title: Do all sedatives promote biological sleep EEG patterns? A machine learning framework
papers.authors: Ramaswamy SM et al.
papers.question: Does a classifier trained on sleep EEG stage sedated EEG?
papers.tried: A 44-feature sleep stager trained on the MGH sleep set (N=994) applied to propofol (36), sevoflurane (36) and dexmedetomidine (30).
papers.method_data: A 44-feature sleep stager trained on the MGH sleep set (N=994) applied to propofol (36), sevoflurane (36) and dexmedetomidine (30).
papers.key_results: Sleep-trained stager on propofol and sevoflurane: AUC 0.55-0.58; dexmedetomidine 0.80.
papers.limits: One multivariate model, one direction; no per-measure test, spectral baseline or surrogate.
papers.ideas_for_us: The prior to cite for #5: sleep-to-propofol transfer of a multivariate stager fails.

papers.title: An electrophysiological marker of arousal level in humans
papers.authors: Lendner JD et al.
papers.question: Is the aperiodic slope a marker of arousal across sleep and anaesthesia?
papers.tried: Spectral slope in scalp and intracranial data across wake, NREM, REM and propofol.
papers.method_data: Spectral slope in scalp and intracranial data across wake, NREM, REM and propofol.
papers.key_results: Per-contrast LDA: wake vs propofol 76.6%, wake vs REM 76.3%, wake vs N3 73.1%.
papers.limits: Separate classifier per contrast; no shared threshold or transfer.
papers.ideas_for_us: Our REM-placement test uses frozen cutoffs, which Lendner did not.

papers.title: Spectral mapping reveals a resemblance of the anesthetic brain state to both sleep and coma
papers.authors: Helfrich JD et al.
papers.question: Which natural state does propofol EEG resemble?
papers.tried: Whole-head spectral maps of propofol (35) correlated with wake, SWS, REM and coma.
papers.method_data: Whole-head spectral maps of propofol (35) correlated with wake, SWS, REM and coma.
papers.key_results: Propofol resembles coma most; its reduced aperiodic activity partly overlaps REM.
papers.limits: Similarity analysis; no classifier transfer.
papers.ideas_for_us: Background: propofol is not simply sleep-like.

papers.title: Atlas of intracranial EEG complexity across cortical regions and global states of consciousness
papers.authors: Jeantin L et al.
papers.question: How does iEEG complexity vary across regions and states?
papers.tried: Kolmogorov complexity, permutation and spectral entropy in 106 iEEG participants; propofol in 5.
papers.method_data: Kolmogorov complexity, permutation and spectral entropy in 106 iEEG participants; propofol in 5.
papers.key_results: Random forest on sleep stages micro-AUC 0.90; complexity lowest under propofol (descriptive).
papers.limits: Propofol n=5, not classified.
papers.ideas_for_us: Complexity measures in sleep and propofol, intracranial only.

papers.title: Measuring the dynamic balance of integration and segregation underlying consciousness, anesthesia, and sleep in humans
papers.authors: Jang H et al.
papers.question: Does an fMRI integration-segregation measure index consciousness across states?
papers.tried: Random forest on propofol fMRI datasets; parallel sleep analysis (n=28).
papers.method_data: Random forest on propofol fMRI datasets; parallel sleep analysis (n=28).
papers.key_results: Propofol AUC 0.984, validated across propofol datasets.
papers.limits: Sleep run in parallel, not as transfer.
papers.ideas_for_us: fMRI analogue of cross-state generalisation.

papers.title: Dexmedetomidine produces more sleep-like brain activity compared with propofol in human participants
papers.authors: Krause BM et al.
papers.question: Is sedative unresponsiveness sleep-like?
papers.tried: Intracranial EEG in 34 patients under dexmedetomidine and propofol compared with sleep.
papers.method_data: Intracranial EEG in 34 patients under dexmedetomidine and propofol compared with sleep.
papers.key_results: Dexmedetomidine resembles N2; propofol changes delta less and network entropy more than sleep.
papers.limits: Patients; intracranial.
papers.ideas_for_us: Explains why sleep-to-propofol transfer can fail.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal brain complexity quantifies consciousness outside of perturbation paradigms
papers.authors: Breyton M et al.
papers.question: Can model-based fluidity track consciousness without TMS?
papers.tried: Whole-brain modelling with fluidity metrics, 15 anaesthesia subjects.
papers.method_data: Whole-brain modelling with fluidity metrics, 15 anaesthesia subjects.
papers.key_results: Fluidity tracks propofol, xenon and ketamine and agrees with PCI.
papers.limits: No sleep.
papers.ideas_for_us: Context for spontaneous-activity complexity measures.

papers.title: The temporal asymmetry of cortical dynamics as a signature of brain states
papers.authors: Camassa A et al.
papers.question: Does irreversibility index brain state?
papers.tried: Rat field potentials across anaesthesia depth and sleep.
papers.method_data: Rat field potentials across anaesthesia depth and sleep.
papers.key_results: Irreversibility lowest in deep anaesthesia and slow-wave sleep.
papers.limits: Rat only; abstract read.
papers.ideas_for_us: Source of the ne2 form we tested on human scalp EEG (atlas).

papers.title: Cortical functional connectivity indexes arousal state during sleep and anesthesia
papers.authors: Banks MI et al.
papers.question: Do sleep and propofol change connectivity alike?
papers.tried: Intracranial EEG, n=5.
papers.method_data: Intracranial EEG, n=5.
papers.key_results: Connectivity shifts in N2/N3 and propofol unresponsiveness are strikingly similar.
papers.limits: n=5, descriptive; abstract read.
papers.ideas_for_us: Background for cross-state transfer.

papers.title: Evaluation of putative signatures of consciousness using specific definitions of responsiveness, connectedness, and consciousness
papers.authors: Casey CP, Tanabe S, Farahbakhsh ZZ, Parker M, Bo A, et al. (Sanders RD senior)
papers.question: Do EEG markers that were built using 'unresponsive' as a stand-in for 'unconscious' actually track experience, or only contact with the outside world?
papers.tried: Ten published resting-state markers (complexity, connectivity, cross-frequency coupling, graph measures, spectrum) scored against serial-awakening reports, split into connected, disconnected-but-experiencing, and unconscious.
papers.method_data: UNCCIOUS study (NCT03284307): dexmedetomidine sedation, propofol sedation and natural sleep, with repeated awakenings and interviews.
papers.key_results: None of the markers tracked experience alone; each also tracked connectedness, and several tracked connectedness only. Front-to-back symbolic transfer entropy tracked connectedness in all three conditions. Going from disconnected experience to unconsciousness lowered permutation entropy and the spectral exponent (P<0.05 in all conditions). (abstract only)
papers.limits: Data on request (IRB discretion), not open; small propofol arm.
papers.ideas_for_us: The closest prior art to our whole benchmark, and it already uses per-awakening reports. It weakens our #5 loose thread (exponent follows slow waves, not experience): here the exponent does separate disconnected experience from unconsciousness. Requesting these data is the best route to a powered sedation-with-reports test.

papers.title: QNodes: A Scalable Algorithm for Efficient Minimum Information Partitioning in Integrated Information Theory
papers.authors: Guerrero Mendieta L, Bustamante-Mora A, Arango-López J, Díaz-Arancibia J, Ossa L
papers.question: Can the minimum information partition, the costly core step in computing IIT's phi, be found fast and exactly for larger systems?
papers.tried: A Queyranne-style pendant-pair search over partitions with the Earth Mover's Distance loss, plus an N-cube representation of conditional distributions, for the effect-side MIP of a mechanism-purview pair.
papers.method_data: Proofs (the loss is symmetric, has a closed form on node-factorizable repertoires, is not submodular in general; exactness holds under a node-by-node checkable condition). Benchmark on 470 subsystems of synthetic and real networks against PyPhi.
papers.key_results: Matched PyPhi's minimum loss in all 317 cases PyPhi completed; 153 times faster at 10 elements; completed every subsystem up to 22 elements. Outside the sufficient condition it is a heuristic, and the paper reports its failure rate and loss gaps against exhaustive search. (abstract only)
papers.limits: Abstract only: the MDPI page and PDF returned HTTP 403. Covers only the effect-side MIP of one mechanism-purview pair, not full system Phi (cause side, purview search, system partition). Exactness is guaranteed only when the condition holds. Modest venue; not yet used by IIT groups.
papers.ideas_for_us: For #9 (phi_proxy): our known-Phi networks are capped by PyPhi's cost. If the code is open, QNodes could extend the ground truth to larger networks for the effect-side quantity only, and its exactness check tells us which networks are safe. Check whether that partial quantity is close enough to system Phi before using it.
papers.source_opened: Crossref metadata and deposited abstract (CC BY 4.0); publisher page and PDF returned 403

papers.title: Is Consciousness a Gradual Phenomenon? Evidence for an All-or-None Bifurcation During the Attentional Blink
papers.authors: Sergent C, Dehaene S
papers.question: Is seeing a target during the attentional blink graded, or all or none?
papers.tried: People rated target visibility on a 21-point scale during the attentional blink, and in a masking task where the target's duration varied.
papers.method_data: Behaviour, about 10 people per experiment. Group rating histograms were fitted by regression as mixtures of the 'absent' and 'seen' histograms.
papers.key_results: In the blink, ratings looked like a mix of two states: unseen and fully seen, with few in between. When masking duration was varied the ratings were one bump that shifted gradually, and in Exp 3 the 'seen' peak itself moved with duration.
papers.limits: Small samples; tested on group histograms, which can hide individual patterns; a bounded rating scale can produce two peaks from a graded signal.
papers.ideas_for_us: The founding behavioural case for all-or-none access. It also shows graded visibility under masking, so a graded result on masking data would not count against the global workspace theory.
papers.source_opened: Opened by the Fable planning agent on 2026-11-23 (prior-art read for Fable list item 4); DOI checked on Crossref

papers.title: Consciousness of targets during the attentional blink: a gradual or all-or-none dimension?
papers.authors: Nieuwenhuis S, de Kleijn R
papers.question: Does the all-or-none pattern in the attentional blink depend on how awareness is measured?
papers.tried: Repeated the blink visibility-rating test, then measured awareness with post-decision wagering and a harder task.
papers.method_data: Behaviour; visibility ratings, wagering.
papers.key_results: With visibility ratings the two-peak pattern came back. With wagering and a harder task it went away, and awareness looked graded.
papers.limits: The authors note that group histograms can blur individual patterns. Depth of reading not recorded by the planning agent, so treated as abstract.
papers.ideas_for_us: The all-or-none shape depends on the measure, which is part of why a behavioural ratings test cannot split theories.
papers.source_opened: Opened by the Fable planning agent on 2026-11-23 (prior-art read for Fable list item 4); DOI checked on Crossref; reading depth not recorded, treated as abstract

papers.title: The Attentional Blink Reveals the Probabilistic Nature of Discrete Conscious Perception
papers.authors: Asplund CL, Fougnie D, Zughni S, Martin JW, Marois R
papers.question: During the blink, does lag change how precisely a target is seen, or only whether it is seen at all?
papers.tried: People reported the target's colour on a colour wheel; a mixture model split guesses from precise reports.
papers.method_data: Behaviour, 28 people; continuous-report mixture model.
papers.key_results: Lag changed the chance that the target was encoded, not the precision of what was encoded. The authors read this as discrete, all-or-none perception.
papers.limits: The mixture model assumes a guess state. Cohen, Keefe & Brady 2023 later fitted a single graded model that did better on these same data.
papers.ideas_for_us: The strongest continuous-report case for all-or-none; reanalysed against it by Cohen 2023.
papers.source_opened: Opened by the Fable planning agent on 2026-11-23 (prior-art read for Fable list item 4); DOI checked on Crossref

papers.title: Perceptual Awareness Occurs Along a Graded Continuum: No Evidence of All-or-None Failures in Continuous Reproduction Tasks
papers.authors: Cohen MA, Keefe JM, Brady TF
papers.question: Do failures of awareness in blink, masking, Sperling and retro-cue tasks need an all-or-none 'guess' state?
papers.tried: Compared one continuous signal-detection model against mixture models across several awareness tasks, including Asplund's data.
papers.method_data: Model comparison (BIC) on continuous-report data from several paradigms.
papers.key_results: The single continuous model beat the mixture models across tasks. On Asplund's data it was preferred in 27 of 28 people.
papers.limits: Continuous colour report is not a visibility rating; the conclusion depends on the signal-detection model family.
papers.ideas_for_us: This closes most of the behavioural all-or-none question, so our item 4 would have added a method, not a new answer. We judged it a no-go.

papers.title: Modelling visibility judgments using models of decision confidence
papers.authors: Rausch M, Hellmann S, Zehetleitner M
papers.question: Which models of decision confidence also describe visibility ratings?
papers.tried: Fitted several graded confidence models to continuous visibility ratings in masked orientation tasks with 5 masking intervals (SOAs).
papers.method_data: Behaviour; model comparison; data on OSF gfkta (no licence set).
papers.key_results: Graded models fit the visibility ratings; no discrete-state model was tested.
papers.limits: No all-or-none model in the comparison. Depth of reading not recorded by the planning agent, so treated as abstract.
papers.ideas_for_us: A 5-level masking dataset that could carry a conditional-independence test, but masking is where graded visibility is already conceded.

papers.title: Evidence for discrete-state processing in recognition memory
papers.authors: Province JM, Rouder JN
papers.question: How can a discrete-state account be told apart from a graded one using rating data?
papers.tried: Proposed 'conditional independence': under a discrete-state model, the response distribution in each state keeps its shape across conditions and only the mixing weights change.
papers.method_data: Recognition-memory experiments with confidence ratings across conditions.
papers.key_results: Recognition memory showed the fixed-shape pattern a discrete-state model predicts.
papers.limits: Memory, not perception. The test needs at least 3 conditions and 3 rating categories to have any power.
papers.ideas_for_us: The right statistic for any all-or-none test on visibility ratings. Our planning agent's simulation suggests about 5 strength levels are needed.
