papers.title: Graded Visual Consciousness During the Attentional Blink
papers.authors: Eiserbeck A, Enge A, Rabovsky M, Abdel Rahman R
papers.question: Is awareness in the attentional blink graded when measured with the Perceptual Awareness Scale?
papers.tried: Attentional blink with a 4-point PAS rating on each trial.
papers.method_data: Behaviour and EEG, 32 people; data on OSF e85hn (CC BY 4.0).
papers.key_results: The authors describe awareness as graded; they ran no formal mixture test.
papers.limits: Only two lags plus target-absent, and 4 rating categories, so a conditional-independence test has very little power (7-33% in our planning agent's simulation).
papers.ideas_for_us: The only open blink set with trial-wise ratings found; too few strength levels for a decisive test.

papers.title: Subjective visibility depends on level of processing
papers.authors: Windey B, Gevers W, Cleeremans A
papers.question: Is visibility more all-or-none for high-level than low-level tasks?
papers.tried: The same masked stimuli at 8 durations, judged on either a number (high-level) or a colour (low-level) task, with visibility ratings.
papers.method_data: Behaviour, 20 people.
papers.key_results: The visibility curve was steeper for the number task than for the colour task: more step-like at the higher level.
papers.limits: A steeper curve is not proof of two states; no mixture test.
papers.ideas_for_us: The level-of-processing view predicts the answer depends on the task, which weakens all-or-none vs graded as a clean theory test.
papers.source_opened: Opened by the Fable planning agent on 2026-11-23 (prior-art read for Fable list item 4); DOI checked on Crossref

papers.title: Electrophysiological markers of surprise-induced failures of visual and auditory awareness
papers.authors: Leong EL, Chua YD, Obana T, Asplund CL
papers.question: Which EEG responses go with surprise-induced blindness and deafness, where a rare task-irrelevant surprise makes people miss a probe 300-400 ms later?
papers.tried: Surprise drives a novelty response that steals the resources needed to become aware of the probe.
papers.method_data: 33 adults, visual (SiB) and auditory (SiD) tasks in counterbalanced order; 16-channel OpenBCI EEG at 125 Hz, left-earlobe reference (stored values are microvolts/24). Data and code are open: OpenNeuro ds006394.
papers.key_results: A late parietal novelty positivity locked to the surprise shrank across trials along with the behavioural deficit; early and probe-evoked components differed by modality and did not habituate (abstract only). Their scripts contrast surprise vs standard and probe present vs absent; they do not contrast aware vs unaware probes.
papers.limits: Abstract only (paywalled). Low-density consumer EEG. Few unaware trials: our count from the behaviour files is a median of 3 surprise-induced misses per subject (visual) and 1 (auditory).
papers.ideas_for_us: We planned ds006394 as the discovery set for the hypothesis generator. Our trial counts killed that: too few unaware trials, and the misses are confounded with surprise and trial number (experiments/hypothesis_generator).

papers.title: Evidence accumulation relates to perceptual consciousness and monitoring
papers.authors: Pereira M, Megevand P, Tan MX, Chang W, Wang S, Rezai A, Seeck M, Corniola M, et al.
papers.question: Does the neural evidence accumulation behind detecting a near-threshold touch also drive confidence and awareness?
papers.tried: Awareness and confidence both read out an accumulated evidence signal, not a separate all-or-none event.
papers.method_data: EEG, 62 channels at 1024 Hz, near-threshold vibrotactile detection with confidence, 500 trials per subject, 20% catch trials, staircase; also intracranial and single-neuron data. EEG data open as OpenNeuro ds001785 (18 subjects; about 140-215 hits and 184-259 misses each).
papers.key_results: A hit-vs-miss decoder defines an evidence-accumulation proxy that a leaky accumulator fits and that also tracks confidence. A per-electrode mixed model on the 0.5-1.5 s mean amplitude gives a detection x confidence interaction. Effects are late (>200 ms).
papers.limits: Named components (P50, N80, N140, P3), time-resolved mass-univariate maps and spectral contrasts are not in the main text.
papers.ideas_for_us: The strongest open trial-level seen/unseen EEG set we have. A preregistered, theory-tagged component screen on it is not in the paper.

papers.title: Decoding across sensory modalities reveals common supramodal signatures of conscious perception
papers.authors: Sanchez G, Hartmann T, Fuscà M, Demarchi G, Weisz N
papers.question: Is there a signature of conscious detection that is shared by vision, hearing and touch?
papers.tried: Train a detected-vs-undetected decoder in one sense and test it in another.
papers.method_data: MEG, near-threshold visual, auditory and tactile stimuli in the same participants; two samples (n = 16 and 14).
papers.key_results: Detected vs undetected decoded across modalities, peaking around 400 ms after the stimulus, and this replicated in the second sample.
papers.limits: MEG, small samples; the shared signal is late and widespread, which a commentary reads as a content-free late modulation rather than a specific mechanism.
papers.ideas_for_us: The closest prior art to a cross-sense transfer screen. Late cross-modal transfer is established in MEG, so that alone would not be new; nobody has done it in open EEG into touch.

papers.title: Dissociating perceptual awareness and postperceptual processing: the P300 is not a reliable marker of somatosensory target detection
papers.authors: Schröder P, Nierhaus T, Blankenburg F
papers.question: Does the P300 mark tactile awareness, or the report that follows it?
papers.tried: Decouple report from detection in the task.
papers.method_data: EEG, near-threshold somatosensory detection with two task versions that decouple report.
papers.key_results: The N140 tracked detection in both versions; the P300 difference vanished when report was decoupled.
papers.limits: Abstract only.
papers.ideas_for_us: Supports the early-negativity side in touch. A component screen on ds001785 should expect N140 to survive and the P3 to depend on report demands.

papers.title: The P50 predicts conscious perception under tactile but not electrical somatosensory stimulation in human EEG
papers.authors: Förster J, Vardiero G, Nierhaus T, Blankenburg F
papers.question: Which early somatosensory ERP components predict whether a near-threshold touch is consciously perceived?
papers.tried: Compare mechanical tactile with electrical stimulation.
papers.method_data: EEG, near-threshold somatosensory detection, tactile and electrical stimulation.
papers.key_results: Per the title, the P50 predicts conscious perception under tactile but not electrical stimulation; our prior-art read also reports N80, P100 and N140 effects and a persisting P300 difference (secondary summary, not checked against the text).
papers.limits: Preprint, not peer reviewed; we read only the title and a secondary summary.
papers.ideas_for_us: Early tactile components are candidate positive controls for a ds001785 screen.

papers.title: Perceptual awareness negativity: a physiological correlate of sensory consciousness
papers.authors: Dembski C, Koch C, Pitts M
papers.question: Is there one early ERP correlate of awareness across vision, hearing and touch?
papers.tried: Pool evidence on the visual, auditory and tactile awareness negativities.
papers.method_data: Review.
papers.key_results: Argues for a general 'perceptual awareness negativity' across senses and against the P3b as a correlate of awareness itself.
papers.limits: A review argument; it does not test whether the same pattern transfers across senses, and the negativities differ in topography by sense.
papers.ideas_for_us: The early-negativity prediction a theory-signed screen would test. Sensor-space transfer of the visual or auditory negativity into touch is expected to fail on anatomy alone.

papers.title: ERP and MEG correlates of visual consciousness: the second decade
papers.authors: Förster J, Koivisto M, Revonsuo A
papers.question: What has a decade of ERP and MEG work found about correlates of visual awareness?
papers.tried: Narrative review.
papers.method_data: Review.
papers.key_results: Favours the visual awareness negativity (VAN) over the late positivity as the correlate of visual awareness.
papers.limits: Narrative, not a meta-analysis; Hutchinson et al. 2026 is the quantitative follow-up.
papers.ideas_for_us: Background for which components count as established.

papers.title: Effects of tDCS on the attentional blink revisited: a statistical evaluation of a replication attempt
papers.authors: Reteig LC, Newman LA, Ridderinkhof KR, Slagter HA
papers.question: Does tDCS over left DLPFC change the attentional blink, as an earlier study suggested?
papers.tried: Replicate the earlier tDCS effect with anodal and cathodal sessions and EEG recorded throughout.
papers.method_data: N = 40, two visits (anodal, cathodal), pre/during/post blocks; letter RSVP with T1 red and T2 green at lag 3 or 8; Biosemi 64-channel EEG. Data: OpenNeuro ds001810.
papers.key_results: No tDCS effect on the blink. The authors did not analyse the EEG 'given the absence of a behavioral effect'. Lags 3 and 8 were chosen to give about equal numbers of seen and missed T2 for EEG.
papers.limits: Behavioural paper only; the EEG is unpublished.
papers.ideas_for_us: Our discovery set for the hypothesis generator: the pre-tDCS blocks give about 45 T2-correct and 55 T2-incorrect lag-3 trials per block, and the T2-correct vs incorrect EEG contrast has never been published on this dataset. Outcome is T2 identification, not seen vs unseen.

papers.title: Representational dynamics preceding conscious access
papers.authors: Alilović J, van Moorselaar D, Graetz M, van Gaal S, Slagter HA
papers.question: What in the EEG predicts whether T2 is seen in the attentional blink, and how early?
papers.tried: Multivariate decoding of seen vs unseen T2 and of T1 identity.
papers.method_data: EEG, Biosemi 64 channels, N = 32, attentional blink (same lab as ds001810).
papers.key_results: The T2 P3 is larger for seen T2 while the T1 P3 does not differ; seen vs unseen decodes for more than 900 ms after T2 and above chance before T1; T1 identity decodes more strongly on T2-seen trials (via our prior-art read).
papers.limits: Abstract and secondary summary only.
papers.ideas_for_us: The closest design to our ds001810 screen; its effects are our within-dataset positive controls, not findings.

papers.title: Electrophysiological evidence for a postperceptual locus of suppression during the attentional blink
papers.authors: Vogel EK, Luck SJ, Shapiro KL
papers.venue: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance
papers.question: Where in processing does the attentional blink act?
papers.tried: Compare ERP components across lags.
papers.method_data: ERPs across lags in the attentional blink.
papers.key_results: P1, N1 and N400 survive the blink while the P3 is suppressed (from memory, via our prior-art read).
papers.limits: Compares lags, not seen vs missed.
papers.ideas_for_us: Background for which ERPs should not differ in a T2 identification contrast.

papers.title: Electrophysiological chronometry of graded consciousness during the attentional blink
papers.authors: Eiserbeck A, Enge A, Rabovsky M, Abdel Rahman R
papers.question: Is awareness in the attentional blink all-or-none or graded in the ERPs?
papers.tried: Relate graded visibility to the N170, the visual awareness negativity and the P3b.
papers.method_data: EEG, attentional blink with graded visibility.
papers.key_results: The N170, VAN and P3b all scaled with graded visibility (via our prior-art read).
papers.limits: Abstract or secondary summary only.
papers.ideas_for_us: Counter-evidence to all-or-none ignition; a binary T2 identification label cannot test grading.

papers.title: Neural correlates of consciousness in an attentional blink paradigm with uncertain target relevance
papers.authors: Dellert T, Krebs S, Bruchmann M, Schindler S, Peters A, Straube T
papers.question: Which attentional-blink ERPs track awareness when T2 is not task-relevant?
papers.tried: Make T2 relevance uncertain to separate awareness from task demands.
papers.method_data: EEG, attentional blink with uncertain target relevance.
papers.key_results: The awareness negativity survived when T2 was task-irrelevant; the P3b did not (via our prior-art read).
papers.limits: Abstract or secondary summary only.
papers.ideas_for_us: In ds001810 T2 is always task-relevant, so a P3b effect there cannot separate awareness from report.

papers.title: Temporal dynamics of access to consciousness in the attentional blink
papers.authors: Kranczioch C, Debener S, Maye A, Engel AK
papers.question: Which oscillatory dynamics go with detected vs missed T2?
papers.tried: Time-frequency EEG analysis of the attentional blink.
papers.method_data: EEG time-frequency, attentional blink.
papers.key_results: Detected T2 goes with more fronto-parietal beta and less alpha synchrony, and lower pre-T1 alpha (via secondary citations).
papers.limits: The sign of prestimulus alpha is contested (Petro and Keil 2015; MacLean and Arnell 2011), and the RSVP rate is in the alpha band.
papers.ideas_for_us: Prestimulus alpha should be left unsigned in a ds001810 screen.

papers.title: Perceptual and attentional impairments of conscious access involve distinct neural mechanisms despite equal task performance
papers.authors: Noorman S, Stein T, Fahrenfort JJ, van Gaal S
papers.question: Do masking and the attentional blink block conscious access in the same way?
papers.tried: Equate performance and compare neural signatures.
papers.method_data: EEG, masking vs attentional blink at matched performance.
papers.key_results: The two impair access by distinct neural mechanisms despite equal task performance (title and our prior-art read).
papers.limits: Abstract only.
papers.ideas_for_us: A caution for transfer: an attentional-blink signature need not carry to near-threshold tactile detection.

papers.title: Subjective Visibility Enhances Early Posterior Electroencephalography Decoding of Stimulus Location across Report and No-report Tasks
papers.authors: Gnodde S, Aslanov V, Hogan A, Francken JC, Olcese U, Stein T
papers.question: Does subjective visibility change what EEG can decode about a stimulus, with and without report?
papers.tried: Near-threshold gratings; stimulus-location decoding in report and no-report tasks, split by visibility.
papers.method_data: EEG; gratings, not faces. Preprint: doi:10.64898/2026.04.20.719596 ('Posterior but not frontal neural signatures of subjective visibility in report-independent EEG decoding').
papers.key_results: Visibility enhances early posterior location decoding (about 130-170 ms) in both tasks; no frontal visibility effect.
papers.limits: Location decoding, not an awareness contrast at a fixed ERP window; different stimuli and data.
papers.ideas_for_us: Supports testing the posterior VAN window at fixed SOA in Cohen 2024; not a pre-emption of that test.

papers.title: Uncovering the Mechanisms of Conscious Face Perception: A Single-Trial Study of the N170 Responses
papers.authors: Navajas J, Ahmadi M, Quian Quiroga R
papers.question: Is the N170 larger on single trials when a face at fixed noise is consciously seen?
papers.tried: Faces in noise at a fixed level near threshold; single-trial N170 analysis by report.
papers.method_data: EEG, face detection with report.
papers.key_results: At fixed stimulus noise, seen (supraliminal) faces evoke a larger N170 than unseen ones on single trials.
papers.limits: Report task, so seen vs unseen also differ in report; a different paradigm (noise, not masking).
papers.ideas_for_us: A VAN/N170 seen > unseen effect at fixed SOA in Cohen 2024 would replicate this; it is the expected positive result, not a new one.

papers.title: Brain Dynamics Underlying the Nonlinear Threshold for Access to Consciousness
papers.authors: Del Cul A, Baillet S, Dehaene S
papers.question: Which ERP stages track the nonlinear visibility curve under masking?
papers.tried: Backward masking of digits across SOAs; ERPs with mask-only subtraction; visibility ratings.
papers.method_data: EEG; the source of the SOA-curve bifurcation method Cohen 2024 follows.
papers.key_results: Early ERPs grow linearly with SOA; a late divergence from about 270 ms follows the nonlinear visibility curve (P3-like, frontal-parietal).
papers.limits: Across-SOA curves mix stimulus strength with awareness, the same confound our fixed-SOA test addresses.
papers.ideas_for_us: Ledger C35 baseline. Our fixed-SOA contrast tests whether divergence at a fixed stimulus also starts this late.

papers.title: Decoding EEG Bifurcation Dynamics Around Visual Detection Threshold in No-Report
papers.authors: Nicolacoudis A
papers.venue: Reed College BA thesis (advisor M Pitts)
papers.question: Do EEG decoding dynamics bifurcate around detection threshold without report?
papers.tried: New experiment from the same lab: gratings varying in contrast, no masks, report and no-report.
papers.method_data: EEG, new data (not the Cohen 2024 set).
papers.key_results: Argues that the across-SOA VAN analysis in Cohen 2024 was hindered by overlap with mask responses, which motivated a mask-free design.
papers.limits: Undergraduate thesis, not peer reviewed; different stimuli.
papers.ideas_for_us: Supports holding the stimulus fixed (one SOA) rather than comparing across SOAs; does not pre-empt our test.

papers.title: Early Local Activity in Temporal Areas Reflects Graded Content of Visual Perception
papers.authors: Tagliabue CF, Mazzi C, Bagattini C, Savazzi S
papers.question: Is the VAN graded with rated clarity (PAS) or all-or-none?
papers.tried: ERPs to reduced-contrast stimuli rated on the four-point Perceptual Awareness Scale.
papers.method_data: EEG, own data.
papers.key_results: A VAN (left centro-parietal, 280-320 ms here) and a late positivity both grew gradually with PAS rating.
papers.limits: Contrast varies with rating, so stimulus and awareness are not fully separated; latency differs from the face VAN.
papers.ideas_for_us: Graded VAN with ratings is established; the unseen-side gradient at a fixed stimulus is not.

papers.title: The EEG signature of sensory evidence accumulation during decision formation closely tracks subjective perceptual experience
papers.authors: Tagliabue CF, Veniero D, Benwell CSY, Cecere R, Savazzi S, Thut G
papers.question: Does the centro-parietal positivity track physical or subjective evidence?
papers.tried: Varied physical stimulus strength and collected ratings of experienced strength.
papers.method_data: EEG, own data.
papers.key_results: The link between physical strength and CPP amplitude is mediated by the subjective rating.
papers.limits: Stimulus strength varies; not a fixed-stimulus seen/unseen test.
papers.ideas_for_us: A P3b/CPP seen-unseen difference may be a decision signal; response-locking is the test.

papers.title: The classic P300 encodes a build-to-threshold decision variable
papers.authors: Twomey DM, Murphy PR, Kelly SP, O'Connell RG
papers.question: Is the P300 a unitary event or an evidence-accumulation signal?
papers.tried: Response-locked and stimulus-locked P300 analyses for auditory and visual targets, with accumulation-to-bound model fits.
papers.method_data: EEG, own data.
papers.key_results: P300 reaches a fixed amplitude just before the response; its rate of rise scales with difficulty and explains RT variance.
papers.limits: Detection tasks, not awareness contrasts.
papers.ideas_for_us: Our P3b seen-unseen difference may be a decision signal; candidate response-locked test.

papers.title: Assessing recognition memory using confidence ratings and response times
papers.authors: Weidemann CT, Kahana MJ
papers.question: Can response times stand in for confidence ratings?
papers.tried: Compared RTs and confidence ratings as measures of recognition-memory decisions.
papers.method_data: Behaviour, own data.
papers.key_results: Much of the information in confidence ratings can be recovered from response times.
papers.limits: Recognition memory, not perception; RT is a noisy proxy at the single-trial level.
papers.ideas_for_us: Supports RT as a weak confidence proxy in the Cohen data, which recorded no confidence.

papers.title: Large language models surpass human experts in predicting neuroscience results
papers.authors: Luo X, Rechardt A, Sun G, et al.
papers.question: Can LLMs forecast neuroscience results better than experts?
papers.tried: BrainBench: pick the real abstract versus an altered one; compared LLMs, a tuned BrainGPT and human experts.
papers.method_data: Benchmark built from published abstracts.
papers.key_results: LLMs beat experts; confidence was calibrated; tuning on neuroscience text helped further.
papers.limits: Tests outcome prediction, not theory-conditional likelihoods; memorisation of published abstracts is a live issue.
papers.ideas_for_us: Prior art for our theory ledger: the real-vs-altered format is close to our real-vs-mirrored items, and their leak concerns are ours.

papers.title: Integrated information and predictive processing theories of consciousness: An adversarial collaborative review
papers.authors: Corcoran AW, Haun AM, Dorman R, Tononi G, Friston KJ, Pennartz CMA, INTREPID Consortium
papers.question: How do IIT, neurorepresentationalism and active inference differ, and what will INTREPID test?
papers.tried: Review comparing the three theories and setting out the hypotheses for the multi-site INTREPID experiments.
papers.method_data: Review, no new data.
papers.key_results: States the planned hypotheses and an evidence-integration scheme; no experimental results yet.
papers.limits: No results, so nothing yet to score forecasts against.
papers.ideas_for_us: Source of pending-outcome items for the ledger when INTREPID reports.

papers.title: Evidence accumulation relates to perceptual consciousness and monitoring
papers.authors: Pereira M, Megevand P, Tan MX, et al., Faivre N
papers.question: Do perceptual consciousness and confidence involve evidence accumulation?
papers.tried: Single-neuron recording in posterior parietal cortex (one participant) and EEG in healthy volunteers during near-threshold vibrotactile detection with confidence ratings; accumulation-to-bound model.
papers.method_data: Intracranial microelectrode and EEG, own data.
papers.key_results: Detected stimuli evoked accumulation-like responses, irrespective of motor confounds or task demands; a model with detection = evidence reaching a bound and confidence = distance from the bound reproduced behaviour and neural data.
papers.limits: Tactile, near-threshold detection; one intracranial participant.
papers.ideas_for_us: Covers the seen-vs-unseen response-locked P3b/CPP question at a fixed stimulus, so our item 3 (P3b response-locking on Cohen data) was skipped as established.

papers.title: Perceptual awareness of near-threshold tones scales gradually with auditory cortex activity and pupil dilation
papers.authors: Doll L, Dykstra AR, Gutschalk A
papers.question: Does the auditory awareness negativity need a non-linear threshold, or does it scale with perception?
papers.tried: Awareness tracks a graded signal, in line with signal detection theory.
papers.method_data: MEG, EEG and pupillometry; near-threshold tones, task-relevant vs irrelevant; six-point perception ratings.
papers.key_results: Task-irrelevant tones gave no awareness negativity or pupil dilation. Task-relevant tones gave both, stronger for hits but present for misses, and responses fell gradually with lower ratings.
papers.limits: Read at abstract level only.
papers.ideas_for_us: Graded counterpart to Sergent 2021 in the same modality; motivates graded generators in our bifurcation audit.

papers.title: Cortical evidence accumulation for visual perception occurs irrespective of reports
papers.authors: Stockart F, Msheik R, Robin A, et al.
papers.question: Does evidence accumulation in cortex explain perception without report?
papers.tried: A leaky accumulator explains both detection and confidence, with or without reports.
papers.method_data: sEEG, 29 participants, three preregistered experiments (immediate response, delayed detection, passive viewing).
papers.key_results: High-gamma build-up slope in visual, inferior frontal and insular cortex tracks RT; the ventral visual signal separates seen/unseen, high/low intensity, and confidence levels.
papers.limits: Read at abstract level only.
papers.ideas_for_us: Same group as Sergent 2021, with a graded-accumulation account; relevant to whether single-trial bifurcation and accumulation can be told apart.

papers.title: Distributional assumptions of growth mixture models: implications for overextraction of latent trajectory classes
papers.authors: Bauer DJ, Curran PJ
papers.question: Can mixture models find latent classes when only one group exists?
papers.tried: Non-normal data alone can make multi-class mixtures look optimal.
papers.method_data: Statistical theory of finite normal mixtures plus simulation.
papers.key_results: Multiple trajectory classes are estimated and appear optimal for non-normal single-population data; within-class estimates are largely uninterpretable.
papers.limits: Read at abstract level only; growth-mixture setting, not EEG.
papers.ideas_for_us: The general statistical principle behind our finding that the Sergent 2021 two-state model wins on heavy-tailed or threshold-jittered graded data.

papers.limits: Read at abstract level only.
papers.title: Cortical activity is more stable when sensory stimuli are consciously perceived
papers.authors: Schurger A, Sarigiannidis I, Naccache L, et al.
papers.question: Is cortical activity less variable across and within trials when a threshold stimulus is seen?
papers.tried: Conscious perception goes with a stable activity pattern, as in attractor states.
papers.method_data: Simultaneous MEG and EEG, threshold-level visual stimuli; pattern-similarity on MEG gradiometers; EEG metric also applied to disorders-of-consciousness patients.
papers.key_results: Variability drops after stimulus onset, then diverges by report: seen trials are less variable, coinciding with within-trial stability; stability alone classifies single trials seen/unseen.
papers.ideas_for_us: Direct prior art for round 15 item 4. Their measure is pattern-based MEG; an amplitude-based healthy-EEG version at a fixed stimulus, with a selection-matched null, is not in the abstract.

papers.limits: Read at abstract level only.
papers.title: Neural Variability Is Quenched by Attention
papers.authors: Arazi A, Yeshurun Y, Dinstein I
papers.question: Do alertness and spatial attention reduce trial-by-trial EEG variability?
papers.tried: Attention raises signal-to-noise partly by quenching variability.
papers.method_data: EEG with alerting and spatial cues.
papers.key_results: Cues reduced trial-by-trial variability, specific to visual cortex and larger contralateral to the attended field; larger quenching went with larger behavioural benefit.
papers.ideas_for_us: Main confound for item 4: seen trials may be more attended, so lower variance on seen trials need not be about consciousness.

papers.limits: Read at abstract level only.
papers.title: Trial-wise awareness ratings do not capture the dynamics of masked priming
papers.authors: Berger A, Rohr M, Wentura D, Kiefer M
papers.question: Do trial-wise PAS changes track changes in masked priming?
papers.tried: Awareness ratings drift with practice independently of priming.
papers.method_data: Reanalysis of three masked priming experiments, with and without trial-wise PAS.
papers.key_results: PAS ratings rose with practice, even on catch trials, without matching changes in priming; ratings also altered priming dynamics.
papers.ideas_for_us: For item 3: practice raises reported visibility in general, so prior-showing effects must be item-specific and control trial rank.

papers.title: Bifurcation in brain dynamics reveals a signature of conscious processing independent of report
papers.authors: Sergent C, Corazzol M, Labouret G, Stockart F, Wexler M, King JR, Meyniel F, Pressnitzer D
papers.question: Does single-trial EEG at threshold show a bifurcation into two states (conscious access), and does this hold without report?
papers.tried: Auditory vowel detection in noise at 6 SNRs, active (report) and passive (mind-wandering probes) sessions; MVPA projections modelled trial by trial.
papers.method_data: 20 subjects, EEG. Decoder trained on no-sound vs max SNR, generalised to intermediate SNRs; per 30 ms window, Model 0 (null), Model 2 (unimodal, logistic mean) and Model 3 (two-state mixture) fitted with 5-fold block CV; random-effects BMS with protected exceedance.
papers.key_results: Model 3 protected exceedance above 0.95 from about 250 to 700 ms; the unimodal model had the highest probability from 0 to 250 ms and again from 700 to 900 ms. The bifurcation fit predicted reports (AUC > 0.75) and mind-wandering probe content without report.
papers.limits: The model set has no graded rival with a jittered threshold or heavy tails: our simulation found the comparison calls bifurcation on such graded data (74-98% of studies), fixed once those rivals are added. The early-unimodal period coincides with weak decoding.
papers.ideas_for_us: Source of our bifurcation audit (NOT SPECIFIC), the extended-model fix (FIX WORKS), the SNR-timing study and the real-data Cohen prereg. Data and code on OSF aw3t5 (Dropbox-linked; 11.4 GB preprocessed active).

papers.title: A late meta-stable code of conscious access in the absence of report
papers.authors: Hutchinson BT, Dehaene S, Slagter HA, Pitts MA
papers.question: Without report (and without a P3b), is there still a late, sustained neural code for seen stimuli?
papers.tried: Reanalysis of four no-report EEG datasets with temporal-generalisation (TG) decoding of seen vs unseen.
papers.method_data: Four EEG datasets; per-timepoint decoders, TG matrices, cluster statistics; 0.1 Hz online high-pass in three datasets, baseline -100 to 0 ms, 250 Hz.
papers.key_results: Seen stimuli gave a TG 'square' at about 200-400 ms without report or P3b; read as a single code sustained over time (GNW ignition). For faces, a decoder trained at 200 ms generalised from about 180 to 400 ms.
papers.limits: Latency jitter is raised and rejected in words, not by simulation. Square vs diagonal is judged by eye; the authors call for a quantitative metric. The pipeline's high-pass and baseline are known to create cross-time generalisation (van Driel 2021).
papers.ideas_for_us: Source of round 16 item 2: does jitter across non-stable transient codes reproduce their square under their pipeline?

papers.title: Characterizing the dynamics of mental representations: the temporal generalization method
papers.authors: King JR, Dehaene S
papers.question: How can decoding across train and test times reveal the dynamics of a mental representation?
papers.tried: Simulations of different neural dynamics and the TG matrices they produce.
papers.method_data: Taxonomy of TG patterns (diagonal, square, chains, reactivation) from simulated sources.
papers.key_results: Sustained codes give a square; a chain of transient codes gives a diagonal. Onset jitter smooths the matrix horizontally and vertically.
papers.limits: Asks, but leaves open, which factors make operations appear diagonal or square.
papers.ideas_for_us: Baseline taxonomy for the TG-square specificity simulation.

papers.title: Temporally unconstrained decoding reveals consistent but time-varying stages of stimulus processing
papers.authors: Vidaurre D, Myers NE, Stokes M, Nobre AC, Woolrich MW
papers.question: Does standard TG decoding mistake growing trial-to-trial timing variability for persistent coding?
papers.tried: Simulated a chain of five states with equal durations and increasing onset variability; proposed an HMM-based temporally unconstrained decoder.
papers.method_data: Simulation plus MEG data; standard TG vs a decoder that lets stage timing vary per trial.
papers.key_results: Standard TG suggests an artificial increase in persistence as the trial goes on: apparently stable patterns can come from increasing onset variability of the same code.
papers.limits: Generic simulation, not EEG-scale and not matched to any consciousness study's pipeline.
papers.ideas_for_us: Closest prior art for TG-square specificity; our gap is a pipeline-matched test of Hutchinson 2026's footprint.

papers.title: Testing the generalization of neural representations
papers.authors: Sandhaeger F, Siegel M
papers.question: Can significant cross-condition or cross-time generalisation arise when the underlying codes are orthogonal?
papers.tried: Simulations of signal mixing in EEG/MEG-like data; a test comparing observed generalisation with what identical codes would give.
papers.method_data: Simulation and analytic arguments; proposed identity-expected generalisation benchmark.
papers.key_results: Signal mixing and dependencies can drive significant generalisation between orthogonal representations; spurious generalisation is markedly lower than expected under identical codes. High-pass filtering can give below-chance TG.
papers.limits: Does not model latency jitter.
papers.ideas_for_us: Their observed-vs-identity-expected ratio is a candidate pre-set square metric.

papers.title: High-pass filtering artifacts in multivariate classification of neural time series data
papers.authors: van Driel J, Olivers CNL, Fahrenfort JJ
papers.question: Do high-pass filtering and baseline correction distort decoding time courses?
papers.tried: Simulations and EEG data with varied high-pass cut-offs and baselines.
papers.method_data: Decoding and TG under filtering settings.
papers.key_results: High-pass filtering and baseline correction displace multivariate patterns into activity-silent periods, most visibly in TG, even at 0.05 Hz.
papers.limits: Read at abstract level only (bioRxiv rate limit).
papers.ideas_for_us: Secondary arm of TG-square study: filter/baseline ablation.

papers.title: A Spatiotemporal Filtering Methodology for Single-Trial ERP Component Estimation
papers.authors: Li R, Principe JC, et al.
papers.question: How well do Woody-type and spatiotemporal methods recover single-trial ERP latency at low SNR?
papers.tried: Simulations with known latency at a range of SNRs; compares Woody filtering to a spatiotemporal filter.
papers.method_data: Simulated ERPs plus real EEG.
papers.key_results: With the true latency fixed, Woody estimates still spread by about 60 ms SD at -20 dB and 15 ms at 12 dB: at low SNR the estimator reports noise as jitter.
papers.limits: Simulation SNRs are not ours; single component.
papers.ideas_for_us: Why the latency-spread study calibrates against each subject's own noise instead of reading a raw lag SD.

papers.title: Single-Trial Mechanisms Underlying Changes in Averaged P300 ERP Amplitude and Latency in Military Service Members After Combat Deployment
papers.authors: Trongnetrpunya A, Rapp P, Wang C, et al.
papers.question: Do averaged P300 changes come from single-trial amplitude or latency changes?
papers.tried: Single-trial P300 latency and amplitude estimation before and after deployment.
papers.method_data: Oddball EEG in service members.
papers.key_results: Separates amplitude from latency effects in averages; warns that the maximum-correlation lag can come from a signal component that is due to noise.
papers.limits: Clinical sample; not masking.
papers.ideas_for_us: Noise-driven lag bias, the same issue our calibration ladder handles.

papers.title: Adiposity influences intraindividual variability in behavioral and neuroelectric indices of attentional inhibition
papers.authors: Kim J, et al.
papers.question: Is intraindividual variability in P3b latency linked to adiposity?
papers.tried: RIDE-based single-trial P3b latency in a flanker task; SDs of single-trial latencies.
papers.method_data: Flanker EEG in adults.
papers.key_results: Single-trial P3b latency SDs of about 77-84 ms, not corrected for the estimator's noise floor.
papers.limits: Flanker task, not masking; raw SDs include estimation noise.
papers.ideas_for_us: A published range for raw P3b latency SD, which brackets our 50 and 75 ms cases.

papers.title: Trial-by-trial detection of cognitive events in neural time-series
papers.authors: Weindel G, et al.
papers.question: Can the trial-by-trial timing of cognitive events be recovered from EEG?
papers.tried: Hidden multivariate pattern (HMP) model fitting event onsets per trial.
papers.method_data: Simulations and oddball-type EEG.
papers.key_results: Condition-averaged ERPs are distorted by between-trial time jitter; later components inherit the jitter of earlier ones; HMP recovers by-trial event times.
papers.limits: Assumes a fixed sequence of events; not masking.
papers.ideas_for_us: An alternative to Woody estimation if our gate says the method is blind.

papers.title: Characterizing the brain's dynamical response from scalp-level neural electrical signals: a review of methodology development
papers.authors: Ouyang G, et al.
papers.question: What methods separate single-trial latency variability from ERP averages?
papers.tried: Review of Woody, RIDE and related decomposition methods.
papers.method_data: Review.
papers.key_results: Latency variability smears averaged components; RIDE decomposes stimulus-locked, response-locked and latency-variable parts.
papers.limits: Review; method author's perspective.
papers.ideas_for_us: Our report-block data have response-locked activity, which the single-code ladder does not model (stated as a limit).

papers.title: All-or-none face categorization in the human brain
papers.authors: Retter TL, Jiang F, Webster MA, Rossion B
papers.question: Is face categorization in the brain all-or-none across stimulus strength?
papers.tried: Frequency-tagged EEG with faces at graded visibility; single-trial classification of responses.
papers.method_data: Scalp EEG, fast periodic visual stimulation.
papers.key_results: The graded average response reflects the proportion of absent and full responses: a mixture of all-or-none trials, not a graded single-trial response.
papers.limits: Faces and frequency tagging, not masking SOA curves.
papers.ideas_for_us: States the mixture identity that makes 'tracks the seen rate' follow from any seen/unseen difference, the core of the psychometric-criterion audit.

papers.title: Neural “Ignition”: Enhanced Activation Linked to Perceptual Awareness in Human Ventral Stream Visual Cortex
papers.authors: Fisch L, Privman E, Ramot M, et al.
papers.question: Do ventral visual responses to masked images show an all-or-none jump with recognition?
papers.tried: Intracranial recordings during backward masking at several SOAs, split by recognition.
papers.method_data: Human iEEG (epilepsy patients).
papers.key_results: Recognized trials show a sharp, sustained gamma increase ('ignition') in high-order visual cortex; unrecognized trials do not.
papers.limits: Clinical sample; electrode coverage varies.
papers.ideas_for_us: Background for the single-trial reading of SOA curves; no critique of the psychometric criterion.

papers.title: Initial-state-dependent, robust, transient neural dynamics encode conscious visual perception
papers.authors: Baria AT, Maniscalco B, He BJ
papers.question: What dynamics of slow cortical activity distinguish seen from unseen threshold stimuli?
papers.tried: Dynamic-pattern (state-space) analysis of whole-brain slow (<5 Hz) MEG during a threshold visual task; across-trial variability split into norm and angle.
papers.method_data: Human MEG, threshold-level visual detection.
papers.key_results: Pre-stimulus patterns predict later seen reports; seen and unseen trials follow separated trajectories; stimulus-induced across-trial variability reduction is mainly in pattern angle, matching Schurger 2015; 5-15 Hz trajectories slow down only in seen trials.
papers.limits: Partly replicates Schurger's across-trial effect; no amplitude- or SNR-matched control of the angle measure.
papers.ideas_for_us: Their 'angle, not norm' result has the same SNR blind spot as Schurger's norm control; the injection test applies to it too.

papers.title: General Markers of Conscious Visual Perception and Their Timing
papers.authors: Rutiku R, Aru J, Bachmann T
papers.question: How variable are the onset times of EEG markers of conscious perception within one study?
papers.tried: Seen vs unseen contrasts on 100 balanced subsets of heterogeneous threshold-contrast stimuli.
papers.method_data: Human EEG, threshold-contrast visual stimuli.
papers.key_results: N200 and P300 are the reliable general markers; their onset varies strongly across subsets; they argue that unseen-trial instability (Schurger 2015) changes how seen/unseen contrasts behave.
papers.limits: Raises the stability-comparison worry but does not test whether stability differences reduce to amplitude or SNR.
papers.ideas_for_us: Prior statement of the concern our injection test settles.

papers.title: Neural activity patterns stabilize during wakefulness and conscious experience
papers.authors: van Gaal S
papers.question: Is stable neural activity a common marker of wakefulness and of conscious content?
papers.tried: Primer on Leung et al.'s preregistered fly study (>7,700 time-series markers across wake, sleep and anaesthesia), linked to human stability findings (King, Schurger).
papers.method_data: Commentary; fly LFP study plus human MEG literature.
papers.key_results: Autocorrelation (stable, consistent processing) best marks loss of consciousness in flies; argues stable, sustained patterns are a cross-species marker of arousal and conscious content, plausibly from long-range recurrence.
papers.limits: Commentary; does not address whether stability measures are confounded by evoked amplitude or SNR.
papers.ideas_for_us: Shows how widely 'stability' is now used as a marker, which raises the value of a specificity test.

papers.title: Alpha entrainment is responsible for the attentional blink phenomenon
papers.authors: Zauner A, Fellinger R, Gross J, Hanslmayr S, Shapiro K, Gruber W, Müller S, Klimesch W
papers.question: Is entrainment of alpha to the ~10 Hz RSVP stream the cause of the attentional blink?
papers.tried: EEG during a 10 Hz RSVP blink task (fixed and jittered SOA); phase-locking index (7-cycle Morlet, 8-12 Hz) within +/-50 ms of T2, AB vs NoAB vs control trials.
papers.method_data: Human EEG, 14 analysed subjects, lag about 300 ms.
papers.key_results: Alpha phase-locking and evoked alpha larger for AB (T2 missed) than NoAB trials at T2; no whole-power difference; concludes entrainment 'may be considered the critical factor'.
papers.limits: 14 subjects; ROI electrodes chosen from the data; the control comparison was not count-matched although PLI depends on trial count.
papers.ideas_for_us: Claim tested by the rhythm_blink study on ds001810 (42 subjects, count-matched).

papers.title: Individual differences in dual-target RSVP task performance relate to entrainment but not to individual alpha frequency
papers.authors: Kranczioch C
papers.question: Do people whose visual cortex entrains more to the RSVP stream show a larger blink?
papers.tried: Between-subject correlations of inter-trial coherence and power with dual-target performance; individual alpha frequency vs stream rate.
papers.method_data: Human EEG, 51 participants.
papers.key_results: Contrary to prediction, ITC correlated positively with performance (for targets not preceded by targets); no mediation by individual alpha frequency.
papers.limits: Between-subject only; no trial-level blink vs no-blink comparison.
papers.ideas_for_us: Opposite-signed evidence to Zauner; its between-subject design is our pre-declared secondary.

papers.title: Endogenous and rapid serial visual presentation-induced alpha band oscillations in the attentional blink
papers.authors: Janson J, De Vos M, Thorne JD, Kranczioch C
papers.question: Are alpha effects in the blink endogenous alpha or the stream's steady-state response?
papers.tried: Blink paradigms with and without 12 Hz pre-target distracter streams; alpha power and intertrial coherence.
papers.method_data: Human EEG.
papers.key_results: Streams raise coherence and lower power; ssVEP-related power tended to be higher when both targets were detected, endogenous alpha lower.
papers.limits: Abstract only; trends.
papers.ideas_for_us: Separates steady-state from endogenous alpha; an opposite-direction trend to Zauner.

papers.title: Pre-target oscillatory brain activity and the attentional blink
papers.authors: Petro NM, Keil A
papers.question: Do pre-target alpha and ssVEP phase locking differ between correctly and incorrectly reported T2?
papers.tried: Pre-T1 alpha power and ssVEP inter-trial phase locking, correct vs incorrect trials, word RSVP.
papers.method_data: Human EEG.
papers.key_results: Incorrect trials: lower alpha power and greater ssVEP phase locking long before T1.
papers.limits: Abstract only; pre-T1 window, which our T2-locked epochs do not cover.
papers.ideas_for_us: Same direction as Zauner but before T1; our test is at T2.
